Ben and Lily were playing in the garden. They liked to dig in the dirt and look for bugs and worms. They had a big bucket to put their finds in.

"Look, Lily, I found a huge root!" Ben said, holding up a long, brown thing. "It's bigger than my arm!"

"Wow, Ben, that's amazing!" Lily said, admiring the root. "Can I see it?"

Ben nodded and handed the root to Lily. She felt how hard and rough it was. She wondered what kind of plant it came from.

Suddenly, they heard a loud yell from the house. It was their mom.

"Ben! Lily! Come here right now!" she shouted. "You made a big mess in the garden!"

Ben and Lily dropped the root and ran to the house. They saw their mom standing on the porch, looking angry. She pointed to the garden, where they had dug up many holes and piles of dirt.

"What were you doing?" she asked. "You ruined the flowers and the vegetables!"

Ben and Lily felt sorry. They didn't mean to hurt the plants. They just wanted to have fun.

"We were looking for bugs and worms, mom," Ben said. "We found a huge root. See?" He showed her the root.

"That's not a root, Ben," mom said. "That's a carrot. You pulled out one of our carrots. And you wasted it. Carrots are food, not toys."

Ben and Lily looked at the root. They realized it was a carrot. They felt silly. They didn't know carrots grew in the ground.

"We're sorry, mom," Lily said. "We didn't know. We won't do it again."

Mom sighed. She was still mad, but she also loved her children. She knew they were curious and didn't mean any harm.

"It's okay, Lily," she said. "But you have to be more careful in the garden. The plants are living things, too. They need water and sun and space to grow. And some of them are for us to eat. You can look for bugs and worms, but don't dig up the plants. Okay?"

"Okay, mom," Ben and Lily said. They hugged their mom and said they were sorry again. Mom hugged them back and smiled.

"Come on, let's go inside and wash up," she said. "Then we can have some carrot cake for snack. How does that sound?"

Ben and Lily smiled. They liked carrot cake. They followed their mom inside, leaving the huge root behind.

Tim and Sam are brothers. They like to play with cars and trucks. They have a big box of cars and trucks in their room. One day, they find a new car in the box. It is red and shiny and has a button on the side.

"Wow, look at this car!" Tim says. "It is so cool! Can I play with it?"

"No, it is mine!" Sam says. "I saw it first! You can play with the other cars."

Tim is sad. He wants to play with the new car too. He waits until Sam is not looking. Then he grabs the new car and runs away.

"Hey, give it back!" Sam shouts. He chases Tim down the hall.

Tim pushes the button on the side of the car. The car makes a loud noise and zooms out of his hand. It flies across the hall and hits the window. The window breaks and the car falls outside.

"Oh no!" Tim says. "The car is gone!"

Sam catches up with Tim. He sees the broken window and the car on the ground. He is very angry.

"You broke the window and the car!" Sam says. "You are so bad! I will tell Mom!"

Tim is scared. He knows he did a bad thing. He starts to cry.

"I'm sorry, Sam!" Tim says. "I just wanted to play with the car!"

But Sam does not listen. He runs to Mom and tells her what Tim did. Mom is very alert. She hears the noise and sees the broken window. She is very mad.

"Tim, what did you do?" Mom says. "You broke the window and the car! You could have hurt yourself or someone else! You are in big trouble!"

Tim feels very bad. He wishes he did not take the car. He wishes he did not break the window. He wishes he did not make Sam and Mom mad. He knows he will not play with cars and trucks for a long time. He has a bad ending.

Tom and Lily are playing in the park. They like to slide, swing and run. They see a big bin with many things inside. They are curious.

"Look, Lily, a bin!" Tom says. "Maybe there are toys or books or snacks inside."

"Let's see, Tom," Lily says. "But be careful. Some things in the bin are dirty or sharp or bad."

They go to the bin and open the lid. They see papers, cans, bottles and boxes. They grab some things and look at them.

"Wow, a can with a picture of a lion!" Tom says. "I like lions. They are strong and brave and loud."

"Ouch, a bottle with a broken top!" Lily says. "It hurts my hand. It is sharp and mean and dangerous."

They drop the things they grabbed and look for something else. They see a box with a shiny ribbon. They think it is a gift.

"Look, Tom, a box with a ribbon!" Lily says. "Maybe there is a toy or a book or a snack inside."

"Let's open it, Lily," Tom says. "But be gentle. Maybe it is someone's gift and they lost it."

They grab the box and pull the ribbon. They open the box and see a cake. It is a chocolate cake with cream and cherries. It looks yummy.

"Wow, a cake!" Tom says. "I like cake. It is sweet and soft and good."

"Me too, Tom," Lily says. "But maybe it is someone's cake and they want it back."

They hear a voice behind them. It is a man. He is angry.

"Hey, you two, what are you doing?" the man says. "That is my cake. I put it in the bin by mistake. Give it back to me now."

Tom and Lily are scared. They drop the box and the cake. They run away from the bin and the man. They are sorry.

"Sorry, mister, sorry," Tom says.

"Sorry, mister, sorry," Lily says.

They go back to the slide, the swing and the run. They do not touch the bin again. They learn a lesson.

The end.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play and sing together. One day, they have a big show at school. They want to make everyone happy.

Anna and Ben practice a lot. They learn a song and a dance. They wear nice clothes and hats. They are ready for the show.

The show starts. Anna and Ben go on the stage. They see many people. They see their parents, their teachers, and their friends. They feel nervous.

"Are you ready, Ben?" Anna asks.

"Yes, Anna. Are you ready?" Ben answers.

"Yes, Ben. Let's do our best!" Anna says.

They smile at each other. They start to sing and dance. They have fun. They do a good job.

The people watch and listen. They like Anna and Ben. They clap and cheer. They say, "Well done, Anna and Ben! You are great!"

Anna and Ben are happy. They bow and say, "Thank you, everyone!"

They go off the stage. They hug each other. They are proud of themselves.

They have a dream. They want to be singers and dancers when they grow up. They know they can do it if they work hard and help each other.

The moral of the story is: You can achieve your dream if you practice, cooperate, and have fun.

Tom and Anna are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big truck with a lot of boxes. The truck stops near the park.

"What is in the boxes?" Tom asks.

"I don't know. Let's go and see," Anna says.

They run to the truck. They see a man with a paper. He is counting the boxes.

"Hello, sir. What are you doing?" Tom asks.

"Hello, kids. I am counting the boxes. I have to deliver them to the shops. They have news in them," the man says.

"News? What is news?" Anna asks.

"News is something that tells you what is happening in the world. Like who is the president, or what is the weather, or if there is a fire, or a new animal, or anything like that. News is in the paper, or on the TV, or on the phone," the man says.

"Wow, that sounds interesting. Can we see the news?" Tom asks.

"Sure, you can have one paper. But be careful, don't rip it or get it dirty. And don't go too far, it is getting dark soon," the man says.

He gives them a paper. They say thank you and run to a bench. They look at the paper. They see a lot of words and pictures. They try to read the words, but they are too hard. They look at the pictures. They see a big building, a big cake, a big dog, and a big smile.

"Look, Tom, this is a big building. It is very tall and shiny. Maybe it is where the president lives," Anna says.

"Look, Anna, this is a big cake. It has a lot of candles and frosting. Maybe it is someone's birthday," Tom says.

"Look, Tom, this is a big dog. It has a lot of fur and a big collar. Maybe it is a new animal," Anna says.

"Look, Anna, this is a big smile. It has a lot of teeth and a big nose. Maybe it is the man who makes the news," Tom says.

They laugh and have fun. They count the pictures. They count one, two, three, four. They are happy. They learn something new. They like the news.

Tom and Lily are best friends. They like to play and joke with each other. Sometimes they tell each other secrets that no one else knows. They whisper in their ears and giggle.

One day, they find a big hole in the ground. It is deep and dark. They wonder what is inside. They decide to make a joke on their teacher, Mr. Fox. They get a rope and a bucket. They put some rocks and dirt in the bucket. They tie the rope to the bucket and lower it into the hole.

They run to Mr. Fox and tell him they have a secret. They say they found something amazing in the hole. They ask him to come and see. Mr. Fox is curious. He follows them to the hole. He looks inside. He sees the bucket. He thinks there is something special in it. He pulls the rope. The bucket comes up. It is heavy. He opens it. He sees only rocks and dirt. He is confused.

Tom and Lily laugh. They say it was a joke. They say they are sorry. They hope he is not angry. Mr. Fox smiles. He says he is not angry. He says it was a funny joke. He says he likes jokes. He says he has a joke for them too. He says he has a secret. He says he has a surprise for them in his classroom. He asks them to come and see. Tom and Lily are excited. They follow him to his classroom. They wonder what it is.

They enter the classroom. They see a big cake on the table. It has candles and frosting. It has their names on it. It is their birthday. They are twins. They forgot. They are happy. They hug Mr. Fox. They say thank you. They say he is the best teacher. They say he has the best joke. They say they love him. They blow the candles and share the cake. They have a great day.

Lila and Ben were playing with their toys in the living room. They had cars, dolls, blocks and books. They made a lot of noise and had a lot of fun.

"Look, Lila, I have a mighty car!" Ben said, zooming his red car on the floor. "It can go very fast and make loud sounds. Vroom, vroom!"

"That's nice, Ben, but I have a mighty sock!" Lila said, holding up a pink sock with a hole in it. "It can be a hat, a scarf, a puppet or a ball. See?" She put the sock on her head, then wrapped it around her neck, then made it talk with her hand, then threw it in the air.

"Wow, Lila, that is a mighty sock!" Ben said, impressed. "Can I play with it too?"

"Sure, Ben, we can share the mighty sock!" Lila said, smiling. "But first, let's rest a bit. We played a lot and we are tired."

"Okay, Lila, let's rest a bit. We can lie on the couch and cuddle with the mighty sock." Ben said, nodding. "But then, we can play some more!"

They went to the couch and lay down with the mighty sock between them. They closed their eyes and felt cozy and warm. They rested for a while, dreaming of more adventures with their toys and their mighty sock.

Anna and Ben are playing with their toys in the living room. Anna has a doll and Ben has a truck. They are having fun, but they are also making a mess. They spill juice on the carpet, they throw pillows on the couch, and they leave their toys everywhere.

"Anna, Ben, time to wash your hands and have lunch!" Mom calls from the kitchen. Anna and Ben do not want to stop playing. They ignore Mom and keep playing.

"Anna, Ben, did you hear me? Come on, now!" Mom says again, louder. Anna and Ben still do not listen. They pretend they do not hear Mom and keep playing.

Mom is angry. She walks into the living room and sees the mess. She is very mad. She yells at Anna and Ben. "Look at this! You made a big mess! You did not listen to me! You are very bad! Go to your rooms, now!"

Anna and Ben are scared. They drop their toys and run to their rooms. They are sorry. They want to say sorry to Mom, but Mom does not want to talk to them. She is too mad.

Mom picks up the toys and puts them in a big bag. She takes the bag to the tip. She throws away the toys. She does not want Anna and Ben to play with them anymore. She thinks they do not deserve them.

Anna and Ben are sad. They cry in their rooms. They miss their toys. They wish they had listened to Mom. They wish they had washed their hands and had lunch. They wish they had not made a mess. They wish Mom was not mad. They wish they could say sorry. But it is too late. Their toys are gone. They have a bad ending.

Leo was a little lion who loved to roar. He roared when he woke up, he roared when he played, and he roared when he was hungry. He roared so loud that all the animals in the jungle heard him.

One day, Leo was roaring near a big tree. He saw a bird with bright feathers on a branch. He wanted to play with the bird, so he roared at it. But the bird was scared of Leo's roar and flew away.

"Come back, bird! I want to be your friend!" Leo shouted.

But the bird did not come back. Leo felt sad and lonely. He wished he had a friend who liked his roar.

Then he heard a noise in the bushes. He saw a little monkey with a long tail. The monkey was curious about Leo and came closer.

"Hello, lion. What are you doing?" the monkey asked.

"I'm looking for a friend who likes my roar. Do you like my roar?" Leo asked.

The monkey nodded. "Yes, I like your roar. It sounds strong and brave. Can I hear it again?"

Leo smiled and roared as loud as he could. The monkey clapped his hands and cheered.

"Wow, that was a great roar! You are a hero, lion!" the monkey said.

Leo felt happy and proud. He had found a friend who liked his roar.

"Thank you, monkey. You are very patient and kind. Do you want to play with me?" Leo asked.

The monkey nodded again. "Yes, I want to play with you. You are fun and friendly. What do you want to play?"

Leo thought for a moment. Then he had an idea.

"Let's play hide and seek. I will count to ten and you hide. Then I will find you with my roar. OK?"

The monkey agreed. He ran to find a hiding spot. Leo closed his eyes and counted to ten. Then he opened his eyes and roared.

"Ready or not, here I come!" he said.

He followed his roar to find his friend. They played hide and seek for a long time. They had a lot of fun. They became the best of friends. They roared and laughed together. Leo was happy. He had learned that his roar was not scary, but special. And he had learned that a friend who likes you for who you are is a true hero.

Sara and Ben are twins. They like to play together. One day, they go with Mom and Dad to a big hotel. The hotel has many rooms and many people.

Sara and Ben see a big cake in the hotel lobby. The cake looks yummy. They want to eat some cake. But Mom and Dad say no. They say the cake is for a party. Sara and Ben are sad.

They wait for Mom and Dad to check in. They see a man with a cart. The cart has many things on it. Sara and Ben see a small cake on the cart. The small cake looks like the big cake. Sara and Ben have an idea.

They run to the cart. They take the small cake. They hide behind a sofa. They eat the small cake. It is yummy. They are happy.

But then they hear a loud voice. It is the man with the cart. He is angry. He says someone stole his cake. He says he needs the cake for the party. He says he will find the thief.

Sara and Ben are scared. They see the man looking around. They see the cake crumbs on their hands and faces. They know they did a bad thing. They feel sorry.

They come out from behind the sofa. They go to the man. They say they are sorry. They say they took his cake. They say they were hungry.

The man is surprised. He sees Sara and Ben. He sees they are twins. He sees they are little. He sees they are sorry. He is not angry anymore. He is kind.

He says it is okay. He says he has another cake. He says he will share some cake with them. He says they can come to the party. He says they can make new friends.

Sara and Ben are happy. They say thank you. They hug the man. They go to the party. They eat some cake. They make new friends. They have fun.

Mom and Dad are proud. They say Sara and Ben are good. They say they are brave. They say they are sorry. They say they learned a lesson.

Sara and Ben smile. They say they love Mom and Dad. They say they love the man. They say they love the cake. They say they love the hotel. They say they love each other.

Jill liked to play with her dolls. She had many dolls, but her favorite was Lily. Lily had a unique dress with flowers and a big bow. Jill always took Lily with her when she went out.

One day, Jill and her mom went to the park. Jill wanted to cross the street and see the ducks in the pond. But her mom said, "No, Jill. You have to wait for the green light. The cars are fast and loud. They can hurt you and Lily."

Jill was sad. She loved the ducks. She looked at Lily and said, "Don't worry, Lily. We will see the ducks soon. Mom will permit us to cross when it is safe."

But then, Jill saw something shiny on the ground. It was a coin. Jill liked coins. She thought, "Maybe I can buy a candy with this coin. Lily would like that." She forgot about the cars and the green light. She let go of her mom's hand and ran to get the coin.

But she did not see the big truck that was coming. The truck honked and screeched. Jill was scared. She dropped Lily and the coin. She tried to go back to her mom, but it was too late. The truck hit her and Lily.

Jill's mom screamed and ran to her. She hugged her and cried. She called for help. Jill was hurt. She felt pain and blood. She looked for Lily, but she could not see her. She said, "Mom, where is Lily? I want Lily."

Her mom said, "I'm sorry, Jill. Lily is gone. The truck broke her. She can't play with you anymore."

Jill was very sad. She wished she had listened to her mom. She wished she had not run for the coin. She wished she had Lily. She said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I love you. You are my unique doll."

Bella was a little girl who liked to play with fire. She thought fire was pretty and warm and fun. She did not listen to her mama and papa, who told her fire was dangerous and could hurt her. They said she should never touch fire or play with matches or candles. They said she should be careful around the fireplace, where they burned coal to keep the house cozy.

One day, when her mama and papa were busy in the kitchen, Bella saw a shiny matchbox on the table. She was curious and foolish. She took the matchbox and ran to the fireplace. She saw some black coal that was not burning. She wanted to make it burn like the other coal. She opened the matchbox and took out a match. She scratched it on the box and it made a spark. She was happy and excited. She brought the match close to the coal and waited for it to catch fire.

But the coal did not catch fire. It was wet and cold. Instead, it made a loud hiss and a puff of smoke. The smoke went into Bella's eyes and made them sting. She dropped the match and cried out. She blinked and blinked, but her eyes still hurt. She rubbed them with her hands, but that made them worse. She was scared and sorry.

Her mama and papa heard her cry and came running. They saw the matchbox and the smoke and the coal and the match. They knew what Bella had done. They were angry and worried. They took Bella to the sink and washed her eyes with water. They hugged her and scolded her. They told her she was very foolish and naughty. They told her she could have burned herself or the house. They told her she should never play with fire again.

Bella felt ashamed and sad. She said she was sorry and she would not do it again. She said she learned her lesson. She said she did not like fire anymore. She said she liked water and ice and snow. She said she would be good and careful. Her mama and papa forgave her and kissed her. They said they loved her and they were glad she was okay. They said they hoped she would remember her mistake and be wise. They said they would get her some eye drops and a bandage. They said they would read her a story and tuck her in bed. They said they would watch over her and keep her safe.

Lily and Ben were playing in the garage. They liked to pretend they were spies on a secret mission. They had a cardboard box as their hideout, and some old toys as their gadgets.

"Shh, we have to be quiet," Lily whispered. "The bad guys are looking for us."

Ben nodded. He held a flashlight and a walkie-talkie. He pretended to talk to their boss. "We found the treasure, boss. It's in the garage. But we need to escape. How do we get out?"

Lily looked around. She saw a big door that led to the backyard. She had an idea. "I know, we can use the bike," she said. "It's fast and quiet. Come on, follow me."

They ran to the bike. It was red and shiny, and had a basket and a bell. It was Lily's bike, and she loved it. Ben was envious. He wished he had a bike like that. He only had a scooter that was old and rusty.

Lily got on the bike and told Ben to hop on the back. She rang the bell and pedaled hard. They zoomed out of the garage and into the backyard. They felt the wind in their hair and the sun on their faces. They laughed and cheered.

"We did it, we escaped!" Lily shouted.

"We're the best spies ever!" Ben agreed.

They rode around the backyard, happy and free. They didn't see the bad guys, or their mom, who was watching them from the window and smiling.

Sara loved to play with her mom's purse. It had many things inside that seemed fun and pretty. She liked to take out the lipstick, the keys, the coins, and the sunglasses and pretend she was a grown-up lady.

One day, Sara saw her mom's purse on the table. She thought her mom was busy in the kitchen and would not mind if she played with it for a little while. She grabbed the purse and ran to her room. She opened the purse and started to take out the things inside.

She put on the lipstick and made a funny face in the mirror. She jingled the keys and imagined she was driving a car. She counted the coins and thought she was rich. She put on the sunglasses and felt very cool.

She was having so much fun that she did not hear her mom calling her name. She did not notice that one of the things she took out of the purse was a small envelope. She did not see that the envelope had a sticker that said "Do not open until your birthday".

Her mom came to her room and saw Sara playing with her purse. She was not angry, but she was surprised. She said, "Sara, what are you doing with my purse? You know you are not supposed to touch it without asking me."

Sara looked at her mom and smiled. She said, "I'm sorry, mom. I just wanted to play with your things. They are so charming. Look, I have lipstick, keys, coins, and sunglasses. And I have this envelope too. What is inside?"

Her mom gasped and took the envelope from Sara. She said, "Oh, Sara, this is a special envelope. It is a gift for you. But you are not supposed to open it until your birthday. It is a surprise."

Sara's eyes widened and she said, "A gift for me? A surprise? What is it, mom? Can I open it now? Please, please, please?"

Her mom shook her head and said, "No, Sara, you have to wait. It is only a few days until your birthday. Then you can open it and see what it is. I promise you, it is something very wonderful. Something you will love."

Sara pouted and said, "But I want to see it now. I can't wait. Please, mom, just a little peek."

Her mom hugged her and said, "No, Sara, you have to be patient. Trust me, it will be worth it. Now, let's put everything back in my purse and go to the kitchen. I have a treat for you. Some cookies and milk. How does that sound?"

Sara nodded and said, "OK, mom. I'm sorry I played with your purse. I love you. And I love your gift. Even if I don't know what it is."

Her mom smiled and said, "I love you too, Sara. And I'm glad you love your gift. But you have to wait until your birthday to open it. It is a secret. A very special secret."

Lily and Tom are twins. They like to play in the farm with the animals. One day, they see a big bag of oats near the barn. They want to feed the oats to the horses.

"Can we take some oats, Mom?" Lily asks.

"Yes, but only a little. The oats are for the horses, not for you," Mom says.

Lily and Tom take a handful of oats each and run to the horse pen. They see a brown horse and a black horse. The brown horse is lying on the grass. The black horse is standing and eating hay.

"Look, the brown horse is sleeping," Tom says.

"Let's wake him up and give him some oats," Lily says.

They go near the brown horse and try to pet him. But the brown horse does not like it. He jumps up and neighs loudly. He scares Lily and Tom. They drop the oats and run away.

"Sorry, brown horse. We did not mean to bother you," Lily says.

The black horse sees the oats on the ground. He walks over and eats them. He thinks they are yummy. He is happy.

"Thank you, kids. You are fair. You gave me some oats too," the black horse says.

Lily and Tom hear the black horse. They stop and look back. They smile.

"You are welcome, black horse. You are nice. You did not scare us," Tom says.

They wave to the black horse and go back to Mom. They tell her what happened. Mom hugs them and laughs.

"You are brave, kids. You learned something new today. Horses have feelings too. Sometimes they want to lie down and rest. Sometimes they want to eat and play. Just like you," Mom says.

Lily and Tom nod. They love the farm and the animals. They want to come back again.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play together. Today, they are at Lily's house. Lily has a new puzzle. It is a modern puzzle. It has many colors and shapes.

"Do you want to play with my puzzle?" Lily asks Ben.

"Yes, please. It looks fun," Ben says.

They sit on the floor and open the puzzle box. They try to find the pieces that fit together. They make a big picture of a city. The city has tall buildings, cars, and people.

"Wow, this is a cool puzzle. I like the city," Ben says.

"Me too. It is a modern city. Maybe we can go there someday," Lily says.

They finish the puzzle and smile. They are proud of their work.

"Let's show it to my mom," Lily says.

They get up and run to the kitchen. Lily's mom is there. She is making a cake.

"Mom, look at our puzzle. We made a modern city," Lily says.

"That's wonderful, Lily and Ben. You did a great job. I'm very proud of you," Lily's mom says.

She hugs them and gives them a slice of cake.

"Thank you, mom. The cake is yummy," Lily says.

"Thank you, Lily's mom. The cake is yummy," Ben says.

They eat their cake and talk about their puzzle. They are happy. They are friends.

Sara and Ben are young. They like to play in the park. They see a big swing. Sara says, "I want to swing, Ben. Can you push me?" Ben nods and says, "OK, Sara. I will push you. But you have to hold on tight."

Sara climbs on the swing and holds on tight. Ben pushes her gently. Sara feels the wind in her hair. She feels happy. She says, "Wee! This is fun, Ben. Thank you for pushing me." Ben smiles and says, "You're welcome, Sara. You are a good sister."

They swing for a long time. They see the birds and the trees. They hear the children and the dogs. They feel the sun and the breeze. The park is peaceful. Sara and Ben are peaceful. They love to swing. They love each other.

Lily loved to skip. She skipped in the park, she skipped in the school, she skipped at home. She liked to skip with her family, too. Her mom, her dad, and her baby brother. They skipped and laughed and had fun.

One day, Lily saw a big dog in the park. The dog was bad. It barked and growled and chased people. Lily was scared. She ran to her mom and dad and held their hands. The dog came near them and tried to bite.

"Go away, bad dog!" Lily's dad shouted. He picked up a stick and threw it at the dog. The dog ran after the stick and left them alone.

"Are you okay, Lily?" Lily's mom asked. She hugged Lily and kissed her cheek.

"I'm okay, mom," Lily said. "But I don't like the bad dog."

"Me neither, Lily," Lily's mom said. "But don't worry, the bad dog is gone now. We are safe."

Lily smiled and nodded. She felt better. She looked at her family and said, "Can we skip again?"

"Of course, Lily," Lily's dad said. "We love to skip with you."

They skipped and laughed and had fun. Lily was happy. She loved her family and they loved her.

Sam likes to play with his toy cars. He has many cars of different colors and sizes. He likes to make them go fast and make noises like a real car. His favorite car is a red one with a big motor. He calls it his original car, because it was the first one he got from his dad.

One day, Sam is playing with his original car in the living room. He makes it zoom around the sofa and the table. He pretends it is racing with the other cars. He is having a lot of fun. But then, he hears a loud bang. He looks at his original car and sees that the motor has broken. He feels sad and angry. He cries and calls for his dad.

His dad comes and sees what happened. He hugs Sam and tells him not to worry. He says he can fix the motor with some glue and tape. He takes the original car to his workshop and works on it. Sam waits and hopes that his car will be okay.

After a while, his dad comes back with the original car. He gives it to Sam and tells him to try it. Sam pushes the car and sees that the motor is working again. He hears the noise and sees the speed. He smiles and thanks his dad. He hugs his original car and calls it his best friend. He is happy again. He and his dad play with the car and the other cars. They have a lot of fun.

Lily and Max were twins who liked to play together. They had many toys, but their favorite was a big vase that their mom gave them. The vase was blue and shiny, and it had flowers on it. Lily and Max liked to pretend that the vase was a castle, a spaceship, or a hat.

One day, they had a fight over the vase. Lily wanted to use it as a castle, and Max wanted to use it as a spaceship. They both pulled the vase, and it broke into two pieces. They were very sad and angry, and they blamed each other.

"Give me the vase, it's mine!" Lily shouted.

"No, it's mine, you broke it!" Max yelled.

They stopped playing and went to their rooms. They did not talk to each other for a long time.

Their mom saw what happened and felt sorry for them. She knew they loved the vase, and she wanted them to be friends again. She had an idea. She glued the vase back together, and put a sticker on it that said "Lily and Max". She brought the vase to their rooms and knocked on their doors.

"Look what I have for you," she said. "It's your vase, and it's fixed. But there is something new on it. Can you see it?"

Lily and Max opened their doors and saw the vase. They were surprised and happy. They saw the sticker with their names, and they smiled.

"It's our vase, and it's beautiful," Lily said.

"Yes, it's our vase, and it's special," Max said.

They hugged their mom and thanked her. Then they hugged each other and said they were sorry. They decided to share the vase and play together again. They were friendly and happy.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a white cat. The cat is very pretty. Anna and Ben want to pet the cat.

But the cat is scared. It runs away from Anna and Ben. It goes into a big box. The box has a hole. The cat goes inside the hole. Anna and Ben follow the cat. They want to say hello.

But the box is a trap. When the cat goes inside, the hole closes. The cat is stuck. Anna and Ben are stuck too. They cannot get out. They are very worried. They cry for help.

A man hears them. He comes to the box. He sees the cat and the children. He is surprised. He opens the box. He lets the cat and the children out. He is very nice. He tells them not to go into traps. He says traps are for bad animals, not for cats and children.

Anna and Ben say sorry. They hug the cat. The cat is happy. It purrs. The man smiles. He gives them a cookie. Anna and Ben say thank you. They learn a lesson. They do not go into traps again. They play with the cat in the park. They are very happy.

Tom and Sam were friends who liked to play soccer. They had a blue ball that they kicked in the park. One day, they saw a big stadium where many people were watching a soccer game. They wanted to go inside and see the game too.

They ran to the gate, but a man stopped them. He said they needed tickets to enter the stadium. Tom and Sam did not have tickets. They felt sad and angry. They saw a hole in the fence near the gate. They thought they could sneak in through the hole.

They set their blue ball on the ground and crawled through the hole. They were inside the stadium. They felt happy and excited. They ran to the seats and watched the game. They cheered for their favorite team.

But soon, another man saw them. He was a security guard. He asked them where their tickets were. Tom and Sam did not have tickets. They felt scared and guilty. The security guard took them to the gate and told them to leave. He also took their blue ball and said they could not have it back.

Tom and Sam walked out of the stadium. They felt sad and sorry. They had lost their blue ball and their chance to see the game. They had done something wrong and they knew it. They wished they had not sneaked in through the hole.

They learned a lesson that day. They learned that they should not try to get something for free that belongs to someone else. They learned that they should respect the rules and the people who work in the stadium. They learned that they should be honest and fair. They also learned that they should take care of their blue ball and their friendship.

Lily and Ben were playing with their toys in the living room. Lily had a big doll and Ben had a small car. Lily liked her doll very much, but she wished she had a car too. She asked Ben if she could play with his car for a while.

"No, this is my car. You have your doll. Go away!" Ben said. He was not very friendly.

Lily felt sad and angry. She wanted to have a car too. She thought of a plan. She saw a bottle on the table. It had a label that said "shrink". She did not know what that word meant, but she thought it might make things smaller. She took the bottle and sprayed some of it on Ben's car.

Ben saw what Lily did and shouted. "Hey, what are you doing? Stop it! You are making my car shrink!"

Lily laughed. She thought it was funny to see Ben's car get smaller and smaller. She picked up the tiny car and put it in her pocket. She said, "Now I have a car too. And you have nothing. Ha ha!"

Ben was very upset. He cried and ran to his mom. He told her what Lily did. Mom was not happy. She scolded Lily and made her give back the car. She said, "Lily, that was not nice. You should not take things that are not yours. And you should not use things that you do not understand. You could have hurt Ben or yourself. You need to say sorry to Ben and share your toys."

Lily felt sorry. She realized she was wrong. She gave back the car to Ben and said, "I'm sorry, Ben. I was mean. I should not have sprayed your car. Can we be friends again?"

Ben was still sad, but he forgave Lily. He said, "It's okay, Lily. I'm sorry too. I should have been more friendly. Can we play together?"

Lily and Ben hugged and smiled. They decided to play together and share their toys. They learned a lesson. They wished they would never fight again.

Lily and Sam are friends. They like to play with toys. Lily has a big doll. Sam has a small car. They share their toys sometimes.

One day, Lily and Sam go to the park. They see a new boy. He has a wide smile. He has a toy train. Lily and Sam like trains. They want to play with the train.

The new boy sees Lily and Sam. He says hello. He is nice. He offers his toy train to Lily and Sam. He says they can play with it. Lily and Sam are happy. They say thank you.

Lily and Sam take turns with the toy train. They make it go fast and slow. They make it go on the grass and on the path. They have fun. The new boy watches them. He has fun too.

Lily and Sam offer their toys to the new boy. They say he can play with them. The new boy is happy. He says thank you. He plays with the big doll and the small car. He likes them.

Lily, Sam and the new boy become friends. They play with their toys together. They share and laugh. They have a wide smile. They are happy.

Tom and Mia are playing with blocks. They like to build towers and houses and cars. But Tom wants to build a big castle and Mia wants to build a small farm. They start to argue.

"Give me that block, Mia!" Tom says. "I need it for my castle!"

"No, Tom, this is my block!" Mia says. "I need it for my farm!"

They pull the block from each other. The block is hard and heavy. It slips from their hands and falls on the floor. It makes a loud noise. It breaks into two pieces.

"Look what you did, Tom!" Mia cries. "You broke the block!"

"It's your fault, Mia!" Tom shouts. "You wouldn't share the block!"

They are both angry and sad. They don't want to play anymore. They turn away from each other.

Mom hears the noise and comes to see what happened. She sees the broken block and the unhappy children.

"What's going on here?" Mom asks. "Why are you fighting?"

Tom and Mia tell Mom their story. They both blame each other. They both want Mom to take their side.

Mom shakes her head. She is not happy. She picks up the broken block and shows it to them.

"Look at this block, Tom and Mia," Mom says. "It was a nice block, but now it's broken. It can't be used for anything. It's not available anymore. Do you know what else is not available when you fight?"

Tom and Mia look at Mom. They don't know what she means.

"Your friendship," Mom says. "Your friendship is like this block. It's precious and valuable. But if you don't share and care for each other, it can break too. And then you won't have anyone to play with or talk to or hug. Is that what you want?"

Tom and Mia shake their heads. They don't want to lose their friendship. They feel sorry for breaking the block and hurting each other.

They look at each other. They see the tears in their eyes and the red marks on their lips. They feel bad.

"I'm sorry, Tom," Mia says. "I didn't mean to break the block or your lip."

"I'm sorry, Mia," Tom says. "I didn't mean to break the block or your lip either."

They hug each other. They say they are sorry again. They smile.

Mom smiles too. She is happy. She hugs them both.

"I'm glad you made up, Tom and Mia," Mom says. "You are good friends. And good friends don't break each other. They help each other and have fun together. Now, let's see if we can fix this block. Maybe we can glue it together. Or maybe we can use it for something else. What do you think?"

Tom and Mia think. They have an idea.

"Maybe we can use it for a bridge," Tom says.

"Or a fence," Mia says.

"Or a slide," Tom says.

"Or a ramp," Mia says.

They laugh. They have many ideas. They are excited.

They take the block and go back to their blocks. They start to build together. They make a castle and a farm and a bridge and a fence and a slide and a ramp. They share and care for each other. They are happy.

Mom watches them. She is proud. She knows they learned a lesson. She knows they won't break their friendship again. She knows they will always be available for each other. She loves them.

Lila and Ben are friends. They live in a small town. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big balloon in the sky. It is red and yellow and blue.

"Wow, look at that balloon!" Lila says. "It is so big and pretty!"

"Maybe it is a magic balloon," Ben says. "Maybe it can take us to a faraway place."

Lila and Ben run to the balloon. They want to touch it. But the balloon is too high. They cannot reach it.

"Maybe we can climb a tree," Lila says. "Maybe then we can get the balloon."

They find a thin tree near the balloon. They try to climb it. But the tree is too thin. It bends and shakes. Lila and Ben fall down.

"Ouch, that hurt!" Lila says. "The tree is too thin. It cannot hold us."

"Maybe we can ask someone for help," Ben says. "Maybe someone has a ladder or a rope."

They look around. They see a man with a big hat. He is holding a string. The string is tied to the balloon.

"Excuse me, sir," Lila says. "Can we have your balloon? We like it very much."

The man smiles. He says, "Sure, you can have my balloon. But you have to do something for me first."

"What do we have to do?" Ben asks.

"You have to believe," the man says. "You have to believe that the balloon is magic. You have to believe that it can take you to a faraway place. You have to believe that anything is possible."

Lila and Ben nod. They say, "We believe. We believe in the magic balloon."

The man gives them the string. He says, "Hold on tight. And don't let go."

Lila and Ben hold the string. They feel the balloon lift them up. They see the town below them. They see the park, the houses, the cars, the people. They see the clouds, the sun, the birds, the stars. They see a faraway place. They see a magic place.

They smile. They say, "Thank you, sir. Thank you for the magic balloon."

The man waves. He says, "You're welcome, kids. Have fun. And keep believing."

Sara and Tom were playing in the snow. They made a big snowman with a hat, a scarf and a carrot nose. They gave him a name: Bob.

"Bob is our friend," Sara said. "He is very nice and cold."

"Yes, he is," Tom agreed. "But we have to go inside soon. It is getting dark and Mom will call us."

They hugged Bob and said goodbye. Then they ran to the house. They left their notebook on the snow. They had drawn pictures of Bob and other snow things in it.

The next morning, Sara and Tom woke up and looked out the window. They saw something that made them sad. Bob was gone. The sun had melted him. There was only a hat, a scarf and a carrot on the ground. And their notebook was wet and soggy.

"Oh no, Bob!" Sara cried. "He was our friend. And our notebook is ruined."

"I know, Sara," Tom said. "I am sad too. But we can make another snowman when it snows again. And we can get a new notebook and draw more pictures."

They hugged each other and felt a little better. Then they went downstairs. Mom had made them hot chocolate and pancakes. They smelled good and tasted yummy. They sat on the couch with a blanket and felt comfortable and warm.

"Mom, can we tell you a story?" Sara asked.

"Sure, sweeties," Mom said. "What is it about?"

"It is about Bob, the snowman," Tom said. "He was our friend, but he melted."

They told Mom their story. Mom listened and smiled. She said she was proud of them for being creative and kind. She said Bob was lucky to have them as friends. She said they could always remember him in their hearts and minds. She hugged them and kissed them. They felt happy and loved.

Lily and Ben were playing in the park with their mom. They liked to swing, slide and run on the grass. They saw some other kids with masks on their faces. They wondered why they had masks.

"Mom, why do they have masks?" Lily asked.

"Because there is a bad germ that can make people sick. The masks help to keep the germ away," mom said.

"Can we have masks too?" Ben asked.

"Sure, I have some in my bag. But you have to wear them all the time when we are outside, okay?" mom said.

She gave them each a mask and helped them put it on. Lily and Ben felt funny with the masks. They could not see their noses and mouths. They could not breathe as well. They could not smile or talk as loud.

They tried to play with the masks, but they did not like them. They wanted to take them off.

"Mom, can we take off the masks?" Lily asked.

"No, sweetie, you have to keep them on. It is for your safety and for others too," mom said.

"But they are not fun. They are itchy and hot and hard to breathe," Ben said.

"I know, honey, but you have to resist the urge to take them off. It is only for a little while. Then we can go home and take them off and have some ice cream," mom said.

Lily and Ben looked at each other. They liked ice cream. They wanted to go home. They decided to listen to mom and keep the masks on. They hoped the bad germ would go away soon. They wanted to play without masks. They wanted to see their friends' faces. They wanted to be happy.

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to play with their toys. One day, they found a microscope in their dad's office. They wanted to see what it could do.

"Let's split this leaf and look at it," Ben said. He tore a small piece of green from a plant and put it on a slide.

"OK, but be careful," Lily said. She turned on the light and looked through the eyepiece. "Wow, I see tiny dots and lines. They are so pretty."

Ben took his turn and nodded. "They are. I wonder what they are."

They heard their dad coming and quickly hid the microscope under a pillow. They pretended to read a book.

"Hi, kids. What are you doing?" their dad asked.

"Nothing, dad. Just reading," Lily said.

"Are you calm today?" their dad asked. He smiled and ruffled their hair.

"Yes, dad. We are very calm," Ben said.

Their dad left and they looked at each other. They giggled and took out the microscope again. They wanted to see more things. They split a hair, a feather, and a crumb. They had fun with their new toy.

Lily was scared of the dark. She did not like to sleep in her big bed alone. She heard noises at night that made her feel cold and shiver. She wanted to be with her mum and dad, but they said she was a big girl and had to sleep in her own room.

One night, Lily had a bad dream. She dreamed that a big monster was under her bed and wanted to eat her. She woke up and screamed. She ran out of her bed and looked for a place to hide. She saw her wardrobe and opened the door. She crawled inside and closed the door behind her. She felt safe in the wardrobe. It was warm and cozy and smelled like her clothes.

"Mum! Dad! Where are you?" she heard a voice outside. It was her dad. He had heard her scream and came to check on her. He turned on the light and looked around the room. He saw her bed was empty and her blanket was on the floor. He was worried. He called her name again.

Lily heard her dad's voice and felt happy. She wanted to see him and hug him. She opened the wardrobe door and peeked out. She saw her dad standing by her bed. He looked at her and smiled.

"Lily, there you are! What are you doing in the wardrobe?" he asked.

Lily came out of the wardrobe and ran to her dad. She wrapped her arms around him and said, "Dad, I had a bad dream. There was a monster under my bed. I was scared. I hid in the wardrobe. I felt safe in the wardrobe."

Dad hugged her back and said, "Oh, Lily, I'm sorry you had a bad dream. There is no monster under your bed. It was just a dream. You are safe with me. Do you want to sleep with me and mum tonight?"

Lily nodded and said, "Yes, please. I love you, dad."

Dad picked her up and said, "I love you too, Lily. Come on, let's go to our bed. You can sleep with us and we will keep you warm and safe."

He carried her to his room and tucked her in between him and mum. Lily felt happy and safe. She closed her eyes and fell asleep. She did not have any more bad dreams.

Anna and Ben liked to play with their toys in the yard. They had many cars, dolls, balls and blocks. Sometimes they shared their toys with their neighbor, Lily, who was very polite and nice. Lily always said please and thank you, and helped them clean up after playing.

One day, Anna and Ben were having a tea party with their dolls. They set up a table and chairs, and poured pretend tea in cups. They invited Lily to join them, and she brought her own doll. They had a lot of fun, pretending to chat and sip tea.

But then, they heard a loud noise. It was Max, the big dog from across the street. Max liked to chase cats, birds and squirrels. He also liked to knock over trash cans, dig holes and bark at people. He was not very polite or nice.

Max saw the tea party, and thought it looked like fun. He ran towards the table, wagging his tail and barking. He jumped on the table, and scattered the cups, plates and dolls. He grabbed one of the dolls in his mouth, and ran away.

Anna, Ben and Lily were very scared and sad. They cried and shouted at Max, but he did not listen. He ran back to his yard, and buried the doll in a hole. He thought he was very clever and funny.

Anna, Ben and Lily went to tell their moms what happened. Their moms were very sorry and angry. They went to talk to Max's owner, and asked him to control his dog. They also asked him to give back the doll, and to pay for the broken cups and plates.

Max's owner was not very polite or nice, either. He said it was not his fault, and that the kids should not leave their toys in the yard. He said he did not know where the doll was, and that he would not pay for anything.

The moms did not like his answer. They said they would call the police, and report his dog. They also said they would not let their kids play with him or his dog anymore.

Anna, Ben and Lily learned a lesson that day. They learned that some people and animals are not very polite or nice, and that they should be careful with their toys. They also learned that they had good moms, who loved them and protected them. They hugged their moms, and thanked them. They also hugged each other, and said they were sorry for losing the doll. They decided to make a new tea party, with new cups and plates, and a new doll. They invited Lily to join them, and they had a lot of fun. They also made sure to keep an eye on Max, and to stay away from him.

Lily and Ben were playing in the living room with their toys. They had a lot of fun making noises and pretending to be animals. Lily had a soft blanket that she liked to cuddle with. She noticed that Ben did not have a blanket of his own.

"Ben, do you want to share my blanket?" Lily asked. "It is very cozy and warm."

Ben smiled and nodded. He took one end of the blanket and wrapped it around himself. He felt happy and snug. He thanked Lily for being so kind.

They continued to play with the blanket, making a tent, a cape, and a scarf. They laughed and giggled. They were having a great time.

But then, Lily saw something that made her sad. There was a small tear in her blanket. She did not know how it happened. Maybe it was from the toys, or the floor, or the couch. She felt a tear in her eye, too. She loved her blanket very much. It was fragile and precious to her.

"Ben, look what you did!" Lily cried. "You ruined my blanket! It has a hole in it! Give it back to me!"

Ben was shocked and scared. He did not mean to hurt the blanket. He did not know what to say. He let go of the blanket and ran away. He felt sorry and sad.

Lily hugged her blanket and sobbed. She wished she had not yelled at Ben. He was her friend and he did not deserve to be treated so badly. She realized that she had been selfish and mean. She wanted to say sorry to Ben and make up with him.

She got up and looked for Ben. She found him in his room, sitting on his bed. He looked lonely and hurt.

"Ben, I'm sorry," Lily said. "I was wrong to shout at you. You did not ruin my blanket. It was an accident. I should have been more careful and gentle with it. And I should have been more grateful and generous with you. You are more important than my blanket. Will you forgive me?"

Ben looked at Lily and saw that she was sincere and sorry. He felt a warm feeling in his heart. He nodded and smiled. He forgave Lily and hugged her.

They went back to the living room and mended the blanket together. They used some thread and a needle that their mom gave them. They made the hole smaller and stronger. They learned to be more careful and gentle with their things. And they learned to be more kind and loving with each other. They were happy and proud. They had a good lesson and a good day.

Tom and Sam are friends. They like to play with cars and balls. One day, they go to the park with their moms. There are many things to do in the park. They can slide, swing, climb, or run.

Tom says, "I want to slide. Sliding is fun. Come with me, Sam." Sam says, "No, I want to swing. Swinging is fun. You come with me, Tom." They do not agree. They choose different things.

Tom runs to the slide. He is careless. He does not look where he is going. He bumps into a girl. The girl falls down. She cries. Tom says, "Sorry, sorry. Are you okay?" The girl says, "No, you hurt me. You are bad." Tom feels sad. He says, "I did not mean to hurt you. I was not looking. I am sorry."

Sam runs to the swing. He is careless. He does not wait for his turn. He pushes a boy. The boy falls off the swing. He cries. Sam says, "Sorry, sorry. Are you okay?" The boy says, "No, you hurt me. You are bad." Sam feels sad. He says, "I did not mean to hurt you. I was in a hurry. I am sorry."

Their moms hear the cries. They come to see what is wrong. They see Tom and Sam with the girl and the boy. They are not happy. They say, "What did you do? Why did you hurt them? You were careless. You have to be careful. You have to say sorry and be nice."

Tom and Sam say sorry to the girl and the boy. They give them hugs. They say, "We are sorry. We were careless. We will be careful. We will be nice. Can we be friends?" The girl and the boy say, "Okay. We forgive you. We can be friends. Do you want to play with us?"

Tom and Sam are happy. They say, "Yes, we want to play with you. What do you want to play?" The girl says, "I want to climb. Climbing is fun. Come with me." The boy says, "I want to run. Running is fun. Come with me." They agree. They choose the same thing.

They all go to climb and run. They have fun. They are careful. They are nice. They are friends. Their moms are happy. They say, "That is good news. You are good friends. You are good kids." They smile. They are proud.

Anna and Tom were going on a big trip with Mom and Dad. They were very happy and excited. They had to pack their bags with clothes and toys and books. Mom and Dad helped them pack. They also gave them a passport each. A passport is a book with your name and picture that you need to go on a plane.

"Look at your passport, Anna. It is very pretty. You are a big girl now. I am very proud of you," Mom said.

"Thank you, Mom. I like my passport. Can I hold it?" Anna asked.

"Sure, but be careful. Don't lose it or drop it. You need it to go on the plane," Mom said.

Anna nodded and held her passport tight. She wanted to show it to Tom. She ran to his room, where he was packing his bag. She opened the door and said, "Look, Tom. I have a passport. Do you have one too?"

Tom looked up and saw Anna holding her passport. He was jealous. He wanted to have a passport too. He did not have one yet. Mom and Dad said he was too little. He was angry and sad. He said, "No, I don't have a passport. You are lucky. You get to go on the plane. I have to stay home with Grandma. It is not fair. Give me your passport. I want it."

He grabbed Anna's passport and tried to take it from her. Anna did not want to give it to him. She said, "No, Tom. It is mine. You can't have it. Let go."

They pulled and tugged and fought over the passport. They did not hear Mom and Dad coming. They did not see the scissors on the floor. They did not notice the passport tearing in half.

Mom and Dad saw what happened. They were very angry and sad. They said, "Oh no. What have you done? You ruined Anna's passport. Now she can't go on the plane. Now we have to cancel the trip. Now we have to stay home. You are very naughty and mean. We are very disappointed in you."

Anna and Tom started to cry. They were very sorry and sad. They wished they had not fought over the passport. They wished they had been nice and kind. They wished they could go on the big trip. But it was too late. The passport was broken. The trip was over. The end.

Sara liked to fold paper. She could make many shapes with paper. She could make a hat, a boat, a bird, and a star. She was proud of her paper shapes. She showed them to her mom and dad. They smiled and clapped.

One day, Sara had a new baby brother. His name was Ben. Sara wanted to show Ben her paper shapes. She went to his crib with a paper hat. She put the hat on his head. But Ben did not like the hat. He cried and kicked. He tore the hat with his hands. Sara was sad and angry. She said, "Ben is rude! He broke my hat!"

Mom heard Sara and Ben. She came to the crib. She saw the torn hat and the crying baby. She said, "Sara, Ben is just an infant. He does not know how to play with paper. He did not mean to be rude. He was scared of the hat. You have to be gentle and patient with him. He will learn to like your paper shapes when he is older."

Sara felt sorry for Ben. She said, "I'm sorry, Ben. I did not want to scare you. I wanted to share my hat with you." She gave him a hug and a kiss. She took another paper and folded a boat. She said, "Look, Ben. This is a boat. It can float on water. Do you want to see?" Ben stopped crying and looked at the boat. He smiled and reached for it. Sara smiled too. She said, "Maybe Ben is not so rude after all. Maybe he is just curious." Mom smiled and said, "That's right, Sara. You are a good big sister. You can teach Ben many things with your paper shapes." Sara and Ben played with the paper boat. They were happy.

Ben and Mia were excited to go to the park with Mom. They liked to play on the swings, the slide and the sandbox. They also liked to see the ducks and the squirrels.

When they got to the park, they saw a big sign that said "Free Vaccines". Mom said they had to get a shot to stay healthy and not get sick. Ben and Mia did not like shots. They were scared of the needle.

Mom took them to a tent where a nice lady was giving shots. She smiled and said, "Hello, I'm Nurse Anna. I'm going to give you a little pinch and then you'll get a sticker and a lollipop. It will be over very fast."

Ben went first. He closed his eyes and held Mom's hand. He felt the needle in his arm and shouted, "Ow!" But it was not very bad. Nurse Anna gave him a sticker of a dinosaur and a lollipop. He said, "Thank you."

Mia saw that Ben was okay. She was brave and went next. She also closed her eyes and held Mom's hand. She felt the needle in her arm and shouted, "Ow!" But it was not very bad. Nurse Anna gave her a sticker of a unicorn and a lollipop. She said, "Thank you."

Mom hugged them and said, "You did great, Ben and Mia. I'm so proud of you. Now let's go have some fun at the park." Ben and Mia smiled and ran to the swings. They were happy and healthy.

Tim and Jen like to swim in the pool. They have fun with the water and the toys. But one day, the pool is broken. There is a big hole in the side and the water is gone.

"Oh no!" Tim says. "The pool is broken! We can't swim now!"

Jen is sad too. She wants to swim and play. She looks around and sees a hose. She has an idea.

"Look, Tim!" Jen says. "We can use the hose to fill the pool again!"

Tim is not sure. He thinks the hole is too big. He thinks the water will come out again.

"I don't think it will work, Jen," Tim says. "The hole is too big. The water will come out again."

But Jen wants to try. She turns on the hose and points it at the pool. The water comes out fast and strong. It makes a loud noise.

"Wow!" Jen says. "It's working! The pool is filling up!"

Tim watches and sees the water rise in the pool. He sees the hole too. He sees the water come out of the hole. He sees the water make a puddle on the ground.

"Jen, stop!" Tim says. "The water is coming out of the hole! The water is making a puddle on the ground!"

Jen hears Tim and looks at the hole. She sees the water come out of the hole. She sees the water make a puddle on the ground. She is surprised.

"Oh!" Jen says. "You're right, Tim. The water is coming out of the hole. The water is making a puddle on the ground."

Jen turns off the hose and drops it. She and Tim look at the pool. The pool is still broken. They can't swim in it.

They are both sad. They don't know what to do.

Then they hear a voice.

"Hey, kids!" the voice says. "What are you doing?"

They turn and see their mom. She is smiling. She has a towel in her hand.

"We were trying to swim in the pool, mom," Tim says. "But the pool is broken. There is a big hole in the side and the water is gone."

Their mom nods. She sees the pool. She sees the hole. She sees the puddle.

"I know, kids," their mom says. "The pool is broken. We have to close it until we can fix it. I'm sorry you can't swim in it today."

Tim and Jen feel sad. They love the pool. They want to swim in it.

"But don't worry, kids," their mom says. "I have a surprise for you. Come with me."

Their mom takes their hand and leads them to the car. She opens the door and tells them to get in.

"Where are we going, mom?" Jen asks.

Their mom smiles and winks.

"You'll see, kids," their mom says. "We're going to a place where you can swim and have fun. A place with no holes and no puddles. A place with a big, blue, beautiful pool."

Tim and Jen feel happy. They like surprises. They like swimming. They like their mom.

They get in the car and buckle up. Their mom starts the car and drives away.

They can't wait to see the place where they can swim and have fun. The place with a big, blue, beautiful pool.

Lily and Tom were playing with blocks. They liked to make towers and houses with the blocks. They had many blocks of different colors and shapes. Some were round, some were square, some were long and some were short.

"Look, I made a big house with square blocks!" Lily said. She was proud of her house. It had a door, a window and a roof.

"That's nice, Lily. But I made a castle with round blocks!" Tom said. He was proud of his castle. It had a wall, a gate and a tower.

They showed each other their blocks and smiled. They were happy to play together.

But then they heard a loud noise. It was a scary noise. It sounded like a roar. They looked around and saw a big dog. The dog was angry. It barked and ran towards them.

"Help! Help!" Lily and Tom cried. They were afraid of the dog. They did not want the dog to bite them or knock down their blocks.

They ran to their mom, who was sitting on a bench. They hugged her and told her about the dog.

"Don't worry, my loves. I'm here. You are safe." Mom said. She was calm and kind. She stroked their hair and kissed their cheeks.

"Can we stay with you, mom?" Lily and Tom asked. They did not want to play with blocks anymore. They wanted to stay with mom.

"Of course, you can stay with me. You can play with something else. How about a book or a puzzle?" Mom said. She took out a book and a puzzle from her bag. They had pictures and words that Lily and Tom liked.

"Thank you, mom. You are the best." Lily and Tom said. They smiled and took the book and the puzzle. They sat on the bench with mom and forgot about the dog. They were happy to stay with mom.

Anna and Ben were playing with their bikes in the park. They liked to ride fast and make loud noises. Anna was older than Ben and she was very bossy. She always told Ben what to do and where to go.

"Ben, follow me!" Anna shouted. "We are going to the big hill!"

Ben did not like the big hill. It was too steep and scary. He wanted to stay on the flat path. But he did not want to make Anna angry. He followed her slowly.

When they reached the top of the hill, Anna smiled. She was proud of herself. She looked down at the slope and said, "Now we are going to ride down as fast as we can. Are you ready, Ben?"

Ben shook his head. He was not ready. He was afraid. He looked at his bike and saw that his pedal was loose. He had an idea.

"Anna, wait!" Ben said. "My pedal is broken. I need to examine it. Can you help me?"

Anna frowned. She did not want to wait. She wanted to ride down the hill. She thought Ben was lying. She said, "No, you don't. Your pedal is fine. You are just scared. Come on, Ben. Don't be a baby. Let's go!"

Ben felt sad. He wished Anna was nicer to him. He wished he had a friend who would listen to him and help him. He said, "No, Anna. I'm not a baby. I'm not scared. But my pedal is really broken. Look, it's wobbly. See?"

Anna looked at Ben's pedal. She saw that it was indeed wobbly. She felt a little sorry for Ben. She said, "Oh, you're right. Your pedal is broken. I'm sorry, Ben. I didn't know. Maybe we should go back and fix it."

Ben smiled. He was glad that Anna saw his pedal. He was glad that she said sorry. He said, "Thank you, Anna. That's very kind of you. Maybe we can ride down the hill another day. When my pedal is fixed. And when I'm ready."

Anna nodded. She realized that she had been too bossy. She realized that Ben had feelings too. She said, "You're welcome, Ben. That's a good idea. And I'm sorry for being too bossy. You are my friend. And I want you to be happy."

Ben and Anna hugged. They got on their bikes and rode back to the flat path. They played together nicely. They had fun. They were happy.

Tom and Anna were playing in the park. They liked to run and jump and slide. They saw a big hill with many trees. They wanted to see what was on the other side.

"Let's go, Tom!" Anna said. "Maybe we can discover something new!"

"OK, Anna!" Tom said. "But be careful. It looks steep and rocky."

They climbed the hill, holding hands. They saw a trail that went into the woods. They followed the trail, curious and excited. They heard a loud roar that made them stop and shiver.

"What was that, Tom?" Anna asked, scared.

"I don't know, Anna," Tom said, brave. "Maybe it's a powerful animal. Maybe it's a lion or a bear or a dinosaur!"

They crept closer to the roar, holding hands tighter. They saw a big cave with smoke coming out. They peeked inside and saw a huge dragon, sleeping on a pile of gold and jewels. The dragon snored and breathed fire.

"Wow, Tom!" Anna whispered. "We discovered a dragon! It's so powerful and shiny!"

"Wow, Anna!" Tom whispered back. "We discovered a treasure! It's so pretty and sparkly!"

They wanted to touch the dragon and the treasure, but they were also afraid. They decided to leave a gift for the dragon, to show they were friendly. They picked some flowers and berries and put them near the cave. Then they ran back to the park, happy and proud.

They told their mom and dad what they discovered. Their mom and dad smiled and hugged them. They said they were very brave and clever. They said they had a wonderful imagination. They said they loved them very much.

Sara and Ben are twins. They like to play with their toys and books. They have many toys and books, because their dad is rich. He works in a big building and wears a nice suit.

One day, Sara and Ben hear a knock on the door. They run to see who it is. It is their grandma. They love their grandma. She always brings them gifts and hugs. She arrives with a big smile and a big bag.

"Hello, my darlings!" she says. "I have something special for you today. Do you want to see?"

Sara and Ben nod and clap. They follow their grandma to the living room. She opens her bag and takes out two boxes. One is blue and one is pink. She gives the blue one to Ben and the pink one to Sara.

"What is it, grandma?" they ask.

"It is a surprise. You have to open it and see," she says. She winks at them.

Sara and Ben open their boxes. Inside, they find two dolls. They are not like their other dolls. They are soft and fluffy and have big eyes and ears. They are bunny dolls.

"Wow!" Sara and Ben say. "They are so cute! Thank you, grandma!"

They hug their grandma and their bunny dolls. They are very happy. They name their dolls Floppy and Hoppy. They play with them all day. They make them jump and dance and talk. They have a lot of fun.

Their grandma watches them and smiles. She is glad to see them so happy. She loves her grandchildren very much. She thinks they are the best gift in the world.

Lily and Tom like to play with blocks. They make buildings with the blocks. They make tall buildings and short buildings. They make houses and shops and schools.

One day, Lily and Tom want to make the tallest building ever. They use all the blocks they have. They raise the building higher and higher. They stand on chairs and books to reach the top. They are very proud of their building.

But then, Ben comes in. Ben is Lily's big brother. He is six years old. He thinks he is very smart. He sees the building and he laughs. He says, "That is a stupid building. It is too tall. It will fall down. Watch this!"

Ben pushes the building with his hand. The building wobbles and shakes. The blocks fall down. They make a loud noise. They hit the floor and the chairs and the books. Lily and Tom are very sad. They cry. They worked hard on their building. They liked their building.

Ben thinks it is funny. He laughs more. He says, "That was a stupid building. You are stupid too. You don't know how to play with blocks. You are babies."

Lily and Tom are angry. They are not stupid. They are not babies. They know how to play with blocks. They say, "You are mean. You are a bully. You broke our building. You are not nice. Go away!"

Ben is surprised. He is not used to Lily and Tom talking back. He is not used to them being angry. He feels bad. He says, "I'm sorry. I was just joking. I didn't mean to break your building. I didn't mean to make you cry. Can I help you make a new building?"

Lily and Tom look at Ben. They are still sad. They are still angry. But they are also kind. They say, "OK. You can help us. But you have to be nice. You have to be careful. You have to share the blocks. And you have to say sorry."

Ben says sorry. He says he will be nice. He says he will be careful. He says he will share the blocks. He helps Lily and Tom make a new building. They make a big building. They make a strong building. They make a beautiful building. They are happy. They are friends.

Bunny was a famous hopper. He could hop very high and very far. He liked to hop all over the forest and show off his skills. He made many friends with the other animals, who cheered for him and gave him carrots.

One day, Bunny saw a hut in a clearing. He had never seen a hut before. He was curious and wanted to hop inside. He hopped closer and closer, until he reached the door. He knocked with his paw, but no one answered. He pushed the door and it opened.

Bunny hopped inside the hut. It was dark and dusty. He saw a big bed, a table, a chair, and a cupboard. He also saw a basket full of food. He smelled honey and bread and cheese. He was hungry and wanted to taste them.

He hopped to the basket and took a bite of the cheese. It was yummy. He took another bite, and another. He did not hear the footsteps outside. He did not see the shadow on the wall. He did not notice the big bad wolf who lived in the hut.

The wolf came in and saw Bunny eating his cheese. He was angry and hungry. He roared and showed his teeth. He wanted to eat Bunny for his lunch. Bunny was scared and sorry. He dropped the cheese and tried to hop away. But the wolf was faster and blocked the door.

Bunny was trapped. He wished he had not hopped inside the hut. He wished he had stayed with his friends in the forest. He wished he had listened to his mother, who told him not to go near the hut. He closed his eyes and waited for the end.

But then, he heard a loud noise. He opened his eyes and saw a big axe. It smashed the door and made a hole. He saw a man with a beard and a hat. He was a woodcutter, who worked in the forest. He saw the wolf and the bunny. He was brave and strong. He swung his axe and hit the wolf. The wolf howled and ran away.

Bunny was saved. He was happy and grateful. He thanked the woodcutter, who smiled and patted his head. He gave him some honey and bread and told him to go back to his friends. He warned him not to hop inside strange huts again. He said goodbye and left.

Bunny hopped out of the hut. He felt lucky and learned a lesson. He decided to be more careful and not to be too curious. He hopped back to the forest and found his friends. He told them what happened and they hugged him and gave him carrots. He was still a famous hopper, but he was also a wiser bunny.

Lily was scared of the dark. She did not like to sleep in her room when the night came. She wanted to stay with Mom and Dad in their big bed. But Mom and Dad said she had to sleep in her own bed. They said she was a big girl now and she had to be brave.

One night, Lily heard a strange noise in her room. It sounded like a growl. She looked around and saw a big shadow on the wall. It had long teeth and claws. It was an unknown animal. Lily was very afraid. She screamed and cried.

Mom and Dad heard Lily's scream and cry. They ran to her room and turned on the light. They saw Lily hiding under her blanket. They saw the shadow on the wall. It was not an unknown animal. It was Lily's teddy bear. It had fallen from the shelf and made the noise and the shadow.

Mom and Dad hugged Lily and told her it was okay. They said it was not a real animal. It was her teddy bear. They said it was her friend and it would not hurt her. They said she could keep it in her bed if she wanted.

Lily felt better. She stopped crying. She took her teddy bear and hugged it. She said sorry to it for being scared. She said she loved it. She said good night to Mom and Dad. They said good night to her and kissed her. They turned off the light and left the room.

Lily was not scared of the dark anymore. She had her teddy bear with her. She closed her eyes and fell asleep. She dreamed of happy things.

Lily liked to dance. She danced in her room, in the garden, and in the park. She made up her own dances. They were original and fun. She felt happy when she danced.

But her brother Ben did not like her dances. He liked to play with his cars and trucks. He did not like the music Lily played. He did not like the noise Lily made. He did not like the way Lily moved. He thought she was silly and weird.

One day, Lily was dancing in the living room. She had a new dance. It was about a butterfly. She wore a dress with wings. She spun and jumped and fluttered. She smiled and sang.

Ben was in his room. He was playing with his cars and trucks. He heard Lily's music. He heard Lily's noise. He heard Lily's voice. He felt angry and annoyed. He wanted Lily to stop. He went to the living room. He saw Lily's dance. He said, "Stop it, Lily! You are stupid and ugly! Your dance is dumb and boring! Go away!"

Lily felt sad and hurt. She liked her dance. She thought it was beautiful and fun. She did not want to stop. She said, "No, Ben! You are mean and rude! My dance is original and creative! I can dance if I want to!"

Ben and Lily started to fight. They yelled and pushed and pulled. They knocked over the lamp and the table. They made a big mess.

Mom heard the noise. She came to the living room. She saw Ben and Lily fighting. She saw the lamp and the table broken. She felt angry and disappointed. She said, "Stop it, Ben and Lily! You are naughty and bad! You have to share and be nice! Go to your rooms and shut the door!"

Ben and Lily stopped fighting. They felt sorry and ashamed. They said, "Sorry, Mom." They went to their rooms and shut the door. They did not dance or play. They sat on their beds and thought. They wished they had been kinder and happier. They wished they had not fought. They wished they could dance and play together.

Lily and Ben are playing with their toys. They have many things to play with: cars, dolls, blocks, and puzzles. Lily likes puzzles. She likes to match the pieces that have the same shape and color. Ben likes cars. He likes to make them go fast and make noises.

"Look, Lily, I have a red car and a blue car. They are very fast and loud. Vroom, vroom!" Ben says.

"Look, Ben, I have a puzzle with animals. They are very cute and quiet. See, this is a cat and this is a dog. They match!" Lily says.

They show each other their toys and smile. They are happy to play together.

But then, the wind blows and the door opens. A cold air comes in. Lily and Ben shiver. They feel cold.

"Brrr, it is cold. I don't like cold. Do you, Lily?" Ben asks.

"No, I don't like cold either. Let's close the door and get a blanket. Then we can play more." Lily says.

They run to the door and close it. They find a big blanket and wrap it around them. They feel warm and cozy. They go back to their toys and play more. They match their puzzles and race their cars. They have fun. They are happy.

Sam and Ben were brothers who liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a big slide with a ladder and a tunnel. Sam wanted to go first, but Ben said he was too weak to climb the ladder.

"I'm not weak, you're weak!" Sam said. He ran to the ladder and started to climb. Ben followed him, but he was slower.

When Sam reached the top of the slide, he saw something shiny in the tunnel. He crawled inside and found a metal spike sticking out of the wall. He touched it and felt a sharp pain in his hand. He cried out and tried to pull his hand away, but the spike was stuck.

"Help! Help!" Sam shouted. Ben heard him and climbed into the tunnel. He saw Sam's hand bleeding and the spike holding it. He was scared, but he wanted to help his brother.

"Sam, don't move!" Ben said. He grabbed Sam's hand and gave it a hard shake. The spike came loose and Sam's hand was free. Sam hugged Ben and thanked him.

"Let's go home, Sam," Ben said. "We need to put a bandage on your hand."

"OK, Ben," Sam said. "You're not weak, you're brave."

They slid down the slide and ran to their mom, who was waiting for them. She saw their faces and knew something had happened.

"What's wrong, boys?" she asked.

"We'll tell you later, Mom," Ben said. "We just want to go home."

They held each other's hands and walked away from the park. They never played on that slide again.

Lily was sad. She had a big cut on her knee from falling down. It hurt and it bled. Mommy put a band-aid on it and gave her a hug.

"Mommy, will it heal?" Lily asked.

"Yes, my love, it will heal. You just need to be careful and not scratch it. It will get better soon." Mommy said.

Lily nodded. She wanted to play outside, but Mommy said she had to rest. She looked out the window. She saw the blue sky, the green trees, and the yellow flowers. She liked the view. It made her happy.

"Mommy, can I have a book?" Lily asked.

"Sure, sweetie, what book do you want?" Mommy said.

Lily thought for a moment. She liked books with animals and colors. She picked one with a soft cover and a picture of a bunny.

"Can you read it to me, Mommy?" Lily asked.

"Of course, my love, let's read it together." Mommy said.

Mommy and Lily cuddled on the couch and read the book. Lily learned new words and saw cute pictures. She smiled and laughed. She forgot about her cut. She felt warm and cozy. She was happy.

Sara liked to eat toast with jam for breakfast. She liked to spread the jam with her knife and make it cover the whole toast. She did not like to leave any white spots. She also liked to cut her toast into small pieces and eat them one by one.

One morning, Sara was making her toast when she heard a loud noise outside. She ran to the window and saw a big truck with a deep hole in the back. The truck was full of dirt and rocks. Sara wondered what the truck was doing. She asked her mom, who was in the kitchen.

"Mom, what is that truck for?" Sara said.

"That truck is for digging a new pool in our backyard, honey," Mom said. "Remember, we talked about it yesterday? We are going to have a lot of fun in the summer."
