Sara nodded. She remembered that Mom and Dad had told her that they were going to build a pool for her and her brother. She was very excited. She wanted to swim and splash and play with her toys in the water.

Sara went back to her toast. She finished spreading the jam and cutting the pieces. She was about to take a bite when she heard another loud noise. She looked out the window again and saw the truck dumping the dirt and rocks into the hole. She gasped. She saw something shiny and red in the dirt. It looked like her favorite toy car. The one that Dad had given her for her birthday.

"Mom, Mom, look!" Sara cried. "My car, my car! It's in the dirt!"

Mom came to the window and saw the car too. She frowned. She remembered that Sara had left it outside yesterday and had forgotten to bring it in.

"Oh, Sara, I'm sorry," Mom said. "That was your car. It must have been in the grass and the truck picked it up. We can't get it back now. It's buried under the dirt."

Sara felt a big lump in her throat. She felt tears in her eyes. She loved her car. She did not want to lose it. She did not care about the pool anymore. She only wanted her car.

She dropped her toast on the plate and ran to her room. She threw herself on her bed and sobbed. She wished she had taken better care of her car. She wished she had not left it outside. She wished the truck had not taken it away.

She hugged her pillow and covered her face. She did not want to see anything. She did not want to hear anything. She did not want to eat anything. She only wanted her car.

Lily and Anna were best friends. They liked to play dress-up with their dolls. One day, they found a big box of old clothes in the attic. They wanted to decorate their dolls with the clothes.

They saw a cool skirt in the box. It was pink and had many flowers on it. Lily and Anna both wanted the skirt for their dolls. They started to pull the skirt from each other.

"Give me the skirt! It is mine!" Lily shouted.

"No, it is mine! I saw it first!" Anna yelled.

They pulled harder and harder. The skirt ripped in half. Lily and Anna both cried. They had ruined the cool skirt.

Their mom heard them and came to the attic. She saw the ripped skirt and the sad girls. She hugged them and said, "Why did you fight over the skirt? You are best friends. You should share and be kind to each other."

Lily and Anna felt sorry. They said sorry to each other and hugged. They decided to use the two halves of the skirt to decorate their dolls. They made two cool skirts out of one. They were happy again.

The moral of the story is: Sharing is caring. Fighting is not nice. Friends should help each other.

Lila and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to swing, slide and run. But it was very hot and sunny. They wanted to find some shade to rest.

"Look, there is a big tree over there!" Lila said. "Let's go and sit under it."

They ran to the tree and saw a hairy animal sleeping on a branch. It was a cat. It had black and white fur and a long tail.

"Hello, cat!" Ben said. "Can we share your shade?"

The cat opened one eye and looked at them. It did not say anything. It closed its eye again and snored.

Lila and Ben sat under the tree and watched the cat. They wondered what it was dreaming about. Maybe it was dreaming about mice or birds or milk.

Suddenly, they heard a loud noise. It was a car. It had a flat tire and stopped near the tree. A man got out of the car. He looked angry and worried.

"Oh no, how will I fix this?" he said. "I have to go to work soon."

Lila and Ben felt sorry for the man. They wanted to help him.

"Maybe we can help you fix your car," Lila said.

"Yeah, we are good at fixing things," Ben said.

The man smiled and thanked them. He gave them a jack and a wrench. They helped him lift the car and change the tire. It was hard work, but they did it.

The man was very happy. He gave them a hug and a candy. He said they were very kind and smart.

"Thank you so much, Lila and Ben," he said. "You saved my day."

The cat woke up and stretched. It jumped down from the tree and rubbed against their legs. It purred and licked their faces. It said they were very brave and friendly.

"Thank you too, cat," Lila and Ben said. "You shared your shade with us."

They all smiled and waved goodbye. Lila and Ben went back to playing in the park. They felt good and proud. They had made a new friend and helped someone in need. They had a great day.

Sara and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to run and jump and slide. They saw a big hill with a lot of trees. They wanted to go up and see what was there.

"Let's go, Sara!" Ben said. "Maybe we can find a secret cave or a treasure!"

"OK, Ben!" Sara said. "But we have to be back before dark. Mommy said so."

They ran up the hill, holding hands. They saw many flowers and birds and bugs. They heard a stream and followed it. They found a big rock with a hole in it.

"Look, Sara! A cave!" Ben said. "Let's go inside!"

Sara was scared. She saw a lot of mist coming out of the hole. She smelled something terrible. She heard a growl.

"Ben, I don't want to go in there!" Sara said. "It's too dark and scary! Maybe there is a monster!"

Ben laughed. He was not scared. He wanted to be brave and have fun. He let go of Sara's hand and ran into the hole.

"Ben, wait!" Sara cried. "Come back!"

But Ben did not come back. He went deeper into the cave. He saw a big shadow and two red eyes. He heard a loud roar. He felt a hot breath and sharp teeth.

He screamed. He was sorry. He regretted going into the cave. He wished he had listened to Sara.

Sara heard Ben scream. She was very worried. She wanted to help him. She ran into the hole. She saw the monster. It was a big bear. It was angry and hungry. It had Ben in its mouth.

Sara was brave. She picked up a stick and hit the bear. She yelled at it. She made it drop Ben. She grabbed Ben's hand and ran out of the cave.

They ran down the hill, back to the park. They were hurt and dirty and scared. They cried and hugged each other.

They saw Mommy waiting for them. She was angry and worried. She saw their wounds and clothes. She asked them what happened.

They told her everything. They said they were sorry. They said they regretted going into the cave. They said they learned their lesson.

Mommy was glad they were safe. She was proud they were brave. She hugged them and kissed them. She took them home. She cleaned their wounds and gave them cookies. She told them she loved them.

They said they loved her too. They said they would never go into a cave again. They said they would always listen to her and to each other. They said they were happy to be home.

Tom and Sue were friends. They liked to play with toys and books. One day, they found a big jar of coins in Tom's house. They wanted to buy more toys and books with the coins.

They took the jar and went to the shop. They saw many things they liked. They gave the coins to the shop man and took the things. They did not count the coins. They did not ask for change. They were happy.

But when they came back to Tom's house, they saw Tom's dad. He was angry. He said, "Where is my jar of coins? I was saving them for a long time. They were very important to me. You took them without asking. You spend them all on foolish things. You are very naughty. You have to give them back."

Tom and Sue were scared. They said, "We are sorry. We did not know. We thought they were for us. We do not have the coins. We have the things. We can give you the things."

But Tom's dad said, "The things are not worth the coins. The coins were more than the things. You made a big mistake. You have to work hard to earn the coins back. You have to return the things to the shop. You have to say sorry to the shop man. You have to learn to be careful and honest. You have to be good friends."

Tom and Sue were sad. They had to do what Tom's dad said. They had to work hard and say sorry. They had to give back the things they liked. They had to lose the coins they found. They had a bad ending. They wished they had not been foolish.

Lily and Tom were playing in the kitchen. They saw a big bowl of fruit on the table. Lily liked fruit. She wanted to eat some.

"Look, Tom, fruit!" Lily said. "Can we have some?"

Tom nodded. He liked fruit too. He saw a green fruit that looked funny. He picked it up.

"What is this?" Tom asked. He smelled it. It smelled sour.

Lily shrugged. She did not know. She saw a red fruit that looked yummy. She picked it up.

"This is a strawberry," Lily said. She bit it. It was sweet and juicy.

Tom wanted to try the green fruit. He bit it. It was bitter and sour. He made a face.

"Yuck!" Tom said. He spit it out. "This is not yummy. This is bad."

Lily laughed. She thought Tom was funny. She wanted to make him laugh more.

"Here, Tom, have another one," Lily said. She pushed the green fruit to Tom. "It is good for you."

Tom did not want the green fruit. He pushed it back to Lily. "No, thank you. You have it."

Lily pushed it to Tom again. "No, you have it."

Tom pushed it to Lily again. "No, you have it."

They pushed the green fruit back and forth. They pushed harder and harder. They did not see the bowl tipping over.

The bowl fell off the table. The fruit rolled on the floor. The juice spilled on the rug. The rug was stained.

Mom came into the kitchen. She saw the mess. She was angry.

"What did you do?" Mom asked. She looked at Lily and Tom. They looked scared.

"We were playing with the fruit," Lily said.

"We did not mean to make a mess," Tom said.

Mom shook her head. She pointed at the green fruit. "Do you know what this is?"

Lily and Tom shook their heads.

"This is a lime," Mom said. "It is not for eating. It is for cooking or making drinks. You wasted a lot of good fruit. And you ruined the rug. You are in big trouble."

Lily and Tom felt bad. They wished they did not play with the fruit. They wished they did not push the lime. They wished they listened to Mom. They said they were sorry. But Mom was still angry. She sent them to their rooms. They could not play anymore. They could not have any more fruit. They had a bad ending.

Lily and Ben were playing in the park after the rain. They liked to jump in the puddles and splash each other. They saw a big puddle that looked like a mirror. They ran to it and gazed at their faces.

"Look, I have a big nose!" Lily said, making a funny face.

"No, you don't. You have a cute nose!" Ben said, smiling.

They gazed some more and saw the clouds and the birds in the puddle. They also saw a man walking his dog. The dog was very big and furry. It barked at them and wagged its tail.

"Hello, doggy!" Lily said, waving.

"Can we pet him?" Ben asked the man.

"Sure, he's very friendly. His name is Max." The man said, stopping by the puddle.

Lily and Ben petted Max and he licked their faces. They giggled and thanked the man. They gazed at the puddle again and saw Max's face too.

"He looks crazy!" Lily said, laughing.

"No, he looks happy!" Ben said, hugging Max.

They gazed some more and saw their own happy faces in the puddle. They decided that puddles were the best mirrors. They said goodbye to Max and the man and ran to find more puddles to play in.

One day, Tom and Anna went to the forest with their dad. Dad wanted to chop some wood for the fire. He had a big axe that was very sharp. Tom and Anna liked to watch him swing the axe and make the wood fall.

"Can I try the axe, dad?" Tom asked. He wanted to be like his dad and chop wood too.

"No, Tom, the axe is too big and heavy for you. You could hurt yourself or someone else. You have to wait until you are older and stronger," dad said.

Tom was sad. He wanted to show dad that he could chop wood. He saw a small axe lying on the ground. It was old and rusty, but it looked like it could still cut. Tom picked it up and tried to swing it.

"Tom, what are you doing? Put that axe down!" dad shouted. He saw Tom holding the small axe and ran to him.

"But dad, I want to chop wood like you. This axe is not big and heavy. It is small and light. See?" Tom said. He swung the axe again, but he did not know how to hold it right. The axe slipped from his hand and flew in the air.

Anna saw the axe flying towards her. She was scared. She screamed and ducked. The axe missed her by a hair and landed on a tree. The tree had a hole in it. Out of the hole came a squirrel. The squirrel was holding a shiny thing in its mouth. It was a rare coin.

"Wow, look at that!" Anna said. She forgot about the axe and ran to the tree. She wanted to see the shiny thing.

"Anna, wait! Don't touch that!" dad said. He followed Anna to the tree. He saw the rare coin in the squirrel's mouth. He knew it was very old and valuable. He wanted to have it.

"Hello, little squirrel. Can I have that coin, please?" dad asked. He tried to be nice and friendly.

The squirrel looked at dad. It did not know what he was saying. It did not want to give up its shiny thing. It ran away with the coin.

"Come back, come back!" dad said. He chased the squirrel.

Tom and Anna watched dad run after the squirrel. They laughed. They thought it was funny.

The end.

Lily is a daughter who likes to wear dresses. She has many dresses in her closet. She is very organized. She puts her dresses in order by color and size.

One day, Lily wants to wear a pink dress with flowers. She looks in her closet and finds it. She takes it out and puts it on. She feels happy and pretty.

She goes to the kitchen to show her mom. Her mom is making breakfast. She sees Lily and smiles.

"Wow, Lily, you look so lovely in your pink dress!" her mom says. "Did you pick it yourself?"

"Yes, mom, I did!" Lily says. "I know where all my dresses are. I am very organized!"

"I am very proud of you, Lily!" her mom says. "You are a smart and neat daughter. Now, come and have some pancakes. They are your favorite!"

Lily hugs her mom and sits at the table. She eats her pancakes and enjoys her dress. She is a happy daughter.

Tom and Sue are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big slide. They want to go on the slide.

"Let's go on the slide!" Tom says.

"OK!" Sue says.

They run to the slide. But there is a problem. The slide is wet. It rained last night. The slide is slippery.

"Be careful!" Sue says.

"I am careful!" Tom says.

But Tom is not careful. He goes too fast. He slides down the slide. He does not stop. He hits the exit. He breaks the exit. He falls on the ground. He hurts his arm.

"Ow! Ow! Ow!" Tom cries.

Sue runs to Tom. She sees his arm. His arm is red. His arm is bad.

"Tom, are you OK?" Sue asks.

"No, I am not OK!" Tom says. "My arm is broken! I need help!"

Sue is scared. She does not know what to do. She looks for help. But there is no one in the park. They are alone.

"Help! Help! Help!" Sue shouts.

But no one hears her. No one comes. Tom and Sue are stuck in the park. They are wet. They are cold. They are sad. They have no fun. They have a bad day. The end.

Sara liked penguins a lot. She had many penguin toys and books. She wanted to see real penguins one day. She asked her mom and dad to take her to the zoo.

At the zoo, Sara saw many animals, but she was most excited to see the penguins. She ran to the penguin pool and watched them swim and play. She saw one penguin that was different from the others. It had a black spot on its chest. Sara thought it was very cute and special.

She saw another penguin that liked the different penguin too. It followed the different penguin everywhere and made funny noises. Sara learned that the two penguins were friends and wanted to marry. She thought that was very sweet and happy.

She asked her mom and dad if she could marry a penguin too. They smiled and said no, but she could love penguins as much as she wanted. Sara said okay and gave them a hug. She said she loved them and the penguins too. She had a very fun day at the zoo.

Tom and Anna liked to play with coins. They had a big jar of coins that their dad gave them. They liked to count them, sort them, and make them shiny. One day, Tom had a new trick. He said he could make a coin vanish.

"Look, Anna, I have a smooth coin in my hand. Do you see it?" Tom said, holding a coin in his palm.

"Yes, I see it. It is silver and round," Anna said, looking at the coin.

"Now, watch carefully. I will close my hand and say a magic word. Then, the coin will be gone!" Tom said, closing his hand and saying, "Abracadabra!"

He opened his hand and showed it to Anna. There was no coin.

"Wow, Tom, you made the coin vanish! How did you do that?" Anna said, amazed.

Tom smiled and said, "It is a secret. Do you want to see it again?"

"Yes, yes, please!" Anna said, excited.

Tom took another coin from the jar and repeated his trick. He closed his hand, said the magic word, and opened his hand. There was no coin.

Anna clapped her hands and said, "That is amazing, Tom! You are a great magician!"

Tom laughed and said, "Thank you, Anna. Do you want to know the secret?"

Anna nodded and said, "Yes, please, tell me!"

Tom leaned closer and whispered, "The secret is... I have another hand!"

He showed Anna his other hand, where he had hidden the coins. Anna gasped and said, "You tricked me, Tom! You are a sneaky magician!"

Tom and Anna giggled and hugged. They put the coins back in the jar and decided to play another game. They had fun with their coins and their magic.

Sara was lonely. She had no friends to play with. She lived in a big house with her mom and dad, but they were always busy. Sara liked to go to the garden and look for bugs. She liked bugs. They were small and funny and made noises.

One day, Sara found a cricket in the grass. It was green and shiny and had long legs. Sara picked it up and said, "Hello, cricket. Do you want to be my friend?" The cricket chirped and jumped in her hand. Sara smiled and put the cricket in a jar. She made holes in the lid so the cricket could breathe. She gave the cricket some leaves and water. She said, "You can stay with me in my room. We can have fun together."

Sara took the jar to her room and put it on her table. She played with the cricket all day. She sang to it, read to it, and drew pictures of it. The cricket seemed happy. It chirped and jumped in the jar. Sara was happy too. She had a friend.

But when the night came, Sara got cold. She put on her pajamas and crawled into her bed. She hugged her teddy bear and said, "Good night, cricket. I love you." The cricket said nothing. It was quiet in the jar. Sara felt sorry for the cricket. She thought, "Maybe the cricket is cold too. Maybe the cricket is lonely too. Maybe the cricket wants to go home."

Sara got out of her bed and took the jar. She put on her coat and shoes and went to the garden. It was dark and windy. Sara shivered. She was scared. She said, "Cricket, where is your home? Where are your family and friends?" The cricket chirped and jumped in the jar. Sara followed the sound. She walked and walked until she came to a bush. She heard many crickets chirping and jumping in the bush. Sara said, "Cricket, is this your home? Are these your family and friends?" The cricket chirped and jumped in the jar. Sara smiled and said, "I understand. You want to be with them. You miss them. I will let you go. But I will miss you. You are my friend."

Sara opened the jar and let the cricket go. The cricket hopped out and joined the other crickets in the bush. It chirped and jumped with them. Sara watched and waved. She said, "Goodbye, cricket. Thank you for being my friend. I hope you are happy. I hope you remember me." The cricket chirped and waved back. It said, "Goodbye, Sara. Thank you for being my friend. I am happy. I will remember you." Sara smiled and turned around. She went back to her house. She was cold and tired, but she was not lonely. She had a friend.

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to play with their toy cars and trucks. They make a lot of noise and pretend they are in traffic.

"Beep beep! Move, move!" Ben says as he pushes his red truck along the floor.

"No, you move! I have a green light!" Anna says as she rolls her blue car next to him.

They both laugh and keep playing. They make turns and stops and honks. They have fun.

But then, they hear a real noise outside. It is loud and scary. They run to the window and look. They see a big fire truck with a siren and a ladder. It is rushing to a house that has smoke.

"Wow! Look at that!" Ben says.

"Is there a fire? Is someone in trouble?" Anna says.

They watch the fire truck stop and the firefighters get out. They see them spray water and climb the ladder. They hope everyone is safe.

They also see something else. Behind the fire truck, there is a small yellow car. It has a cute dog in the back seat. The dog is barking and wagging its tail. It looks happy and friendly.

"Look at the dog! It is so cute!" Anna says.

"I want to pet it! Can we go outside?" Ben says.

They ask their mom if they can go outside. She says yes, but they have to be careful and stay close. They put on their shoes and coats and run outside. They see the dog and wave to it. The dog barks and wags its tail more.

"Hi, doggy! What is your name?" Anna says.

The dog's owner sees them and smiles. She is a nice lady who lives in the house next to the one with the smoke. She says her name is Mrs. Lee and her dog's name is Sunny.

"Sunny is very friendly. Do you want to pet him?" she says.

"Yes, please!" Ben says.

They pet Sunny and he licks their faces. He is soft and warm and fluffy. They giggle and hug him. They make a new friend.

They also see the firefighters put out the fire and save the people in the house. They are brave and strong and helpful. They clap and cheer for them.

They have a big adventure. They see a lot of things. They learn a lot of words. They have a lot of fun.

Lily wanted to mail a picture to her grandma. She drew a big heart and wrote "I love you" with her crayons. She asked her mom for an envelope and a stamp. Her mom helped her put the picture inside and write the address.

"Can we go to the mailbox now?" Lily asked.

"Yes, let's go," her mom said. They put on their coats and shoes and walked to the mailbox. Lily was very happy.

But on the way, Lily saw a juice stand. She loved juice. She wanted to buy some. She asked her mom for some money.

"Sorry, honey, I don't have any money with me. We can have some juice when we get home," her mom said.

Lily was very sad. She wanted juice now. She saw a coin on the ground. She picked it up. She thought maybe she could use it to buy juice. She ran to the juice stand and gave the coin to the man.

"Thank you," the man said. He gave her a cup of juice.

Lily drank the juice. It was very good. She felt better.

But then she remembered her picture. She looked at her hand. She had dropped the envelope. She didn't have it anymore. She felt very bad. She had lost her picture for grandma.

She ran back to her mom. She was crying.

"Mom, I'm sorry, I'm sorry, I lost the picture, I lost the envelope, I found a coin and I bought juice and I dropped it and I'm sorry, I'm sorry," she sobbed.

Her mom hugged her. She was not angry. She was sad too.

"It's okay, Lily, it's okay. I know you didn't mean to. You made a mistake. You were tempted by the juice. But you shouldn't have taken the coin. That was not yours. You should have asked the man if he lost it. You should have been honest. Do you understand?" her mom said.

Lily nodded. She understood. She felt ashamed. She had done something wrong.

"I'm sorry, mom. I'm sorry, grandma. I love you. Can I make another picture?" she asked.

"Of course, you can, Lily. And we can mail it tomorrow. And we can also return the coin to the man. And we can say sorry to him too. And we can learn from this. And we can still have some juice at home. Okay?" her mom said.

"Okay, mom. Thank you, mom. You are the best mom," Lily said.

They hugged again. They walked home. They made another picture. They returned the coin. They said sorry. They had some juice. They mailed the picture. They felt better. They loved each other. The end.

Lily and Ben were friends. They liked to play with toys and run in the park. One day, they went to Ben's house for lunch. Ben's mom made them sandwiches and juice. She said they could have dessert if they ate well.

Lily and Ben ate their sandwiches and drank their juice. They were happy. They wanted dessert. Ben's mom brought a big cake. It had chocolate and cream and cherries. It looked yummy. Lily and Ben smiled.

"Can we have some cake, please?" they asked.

"Yes, you can. But you have to share. The cake is wide. There is enough for both of you," Ben's mom said.

She cut the cake in two pieces. She gave one piece to Lily and one piece to Ben. She put them on plates. She gave them forks and napkins.

"Thank you, mom," Ben said.

"Thank you, Ben's mom," Lily said.

They started to eat their cake. It was sweet and soft and good. Lily and Ben liked it a lot. But Ben wanted more. He looked at Lily's plate. Her piece was bigger than his. He felt angry.

"Hey, that's not fair. Your piece is bigger than mine. Give me some of your cake," Ben said.

"No, it's not. It's the same. And it's mine. You have your own cake. Eat it," Lily said.

They argued. They raised their voices. They did not share. Ben's mom heard them. She came back to the kitchen. She saw them fighting.

"What's going on here? Why are you yelling? Why are you not sharing?" she asked.

Ben did not answer. He was too mad. He wanted Lily's cake. He did not care about his mom. He did not care about being nice. He did a bad thing. He kicked Lily's plate. The cake flew in the air. It landed on the floor. It made a mess.

Lily cried. She was hurt and sad. She did not have any cake. She did not have any friend. Ben's mom was shocked and angry. She did not have any cake. She did not have any fun.

She scolded Ben. She told him to say sorry. She told him to clean up. She told him to go to his room. She told him he could not have any dessert. She told him he was naughty.

Ben did not say sorry. He did not clean up. He did not go to his room. He did not listen. He did another bad thing. He kicked his mom. He hurt her. He made her cry.

Lily and Ben's mom cried. They did not have any cake. They did not have any friend. They did not have any happiness. Ben did not cry. He did not have any cake. He did not have any friend. He did not have any happiness. He only had anger. He was alone. He was bad.

The end.

Lily and Max wanted to decorate their room for winter. They had many stickers, papers, and crayons. They liked to make snowflakes, snowmen, and penguins.

"Look, Lily, I made a big snowman!" Max said. He showed his paper to his sister. "He has a hat, a scarf, and a carrot nose."

"Wow, Max, that's very good!" Lily said. She smiled and clapped. "I made a penguin. He has a black and white coat, a yellow beak, and orange feet."

They put their papers on the wall with tape. They also stuck some stickers of stars, snowflakes, and trees. Their room looked very pretty and cozy.

"Let's check the thermometer, Lily," Max said. He pointed to the window. "Maybe it's cold enough to make real snowmen outside."

They ran to the window and looked at the thermometer. It was a red stick with numbers and a line. The line was very low, near the bottom.

"Brrr, it's very cold, Max," Lily said. She shivered and hugged her brother. "The thermometer says it's minus five."

"Minus five? What does that mean?" Max asked. He tilted his head and frowned.

"It means it's colder than zero," Lily said. She was very smart and organized. She liked to learn new things. "Zero is when water freezes and becomes ice. Minus means less than zero. So minus five is very, very cold."

"Wow, Lily, you know a lot!" Max said. He was very impressed and proud of his sister. "Maybe we can go outside and play in the snow later. But first, let's have some hot chocolate and cookies. Mom said she made some for us."

"Yay, hot chocolate and cookies!" Lily said. She nodded and smiled. "That sounds yummy and warm. Let's go, Max."

They held hands and ran to the kitchen. They left their room decorated and beautiful. They were happy and excited. They loved winter and each other.

Tom and Lily are going to the park with Mom. They live in a big building with many floors. To go down, they have to use the elevator. The elevator is a big box with buttons and doors that can move up and down.

They get in the elevator and Mom pushes the button for the ground floor. The elevator starts to move down. Tom and Lily are excited. They like the park. They can play on the swings, the slide and the sandbox.

But when the elevator stops and the doors open, they see something bad. It is raining outside. The sky is gray and the ground is wet. Tom and Lily are sad. They do not like the rain. They cannot play in the park when it is wet.

"Mom, can we still go to the park?" Tom asks.

"I'm sorry, sweetie, but we can't. It is too wet and cold. We have to go back to our apartment and wait for the rain to stop." Mom says.

"But we want to play!" Lily says.

"I know, honey, but we can play inside. We can read books, draw pictures, or play with your toys. Maybe the rain will stop later and we can go to the park then." Mom says.

Tom and Lily are not happy, but they listen to Mom. They get back in the elevator and Mom pushes the button for their floor. The elevator starts to move up. Tom and Lily hope the rain will stop soon. They still want to play in the park.

Tom and Anna liked to play in the attic. They found many old things there, like toys, books, and clothes. Sometimes they pretended to be pirates, or knights, or fairies. They had a lot of fun.

One day, they saw a big box in the corner. They opened it and saw a lot of bottles. They were curious. They took out one bottle and looked at it. It had a label that said "lemonade". They thought it was a drink.

"Let's try it!" Tom said.

"OK!" Anna said.

They opened the bottle and took a sip. It was very sour. They made a face and spat it out.

"Yuck! This is not lemonade!" Anna said.

"It's vinegar!" Tom said.

They looked at the other bottles. They all said "vinegar". They wondered why someone put vinegar in the attic.

They heard a noise. It was their mom. She was coming up the stairs.

"Tom! Anna! What are you doing in the attic?" she asked.

They were scared. They knew they were not supposed to play in the attic. They tried to hide behind the box.

"Freeze!" their mom said. "Don't move!"

She saw the bottle of vinegar in their hands. She was angry.

"Did you drink this?" she asked.

They nodded. They felt sorry.

"You are very naughty!" their mom said. "This is not for drinking! This is for cleaning! You could get sick!"

She took them downstairs. She gave them water to drink. She told them to go to their room. They had no dinner. They had no dessert. They had no story. They had to go to bed early.

They cried. They learned their lesson. They never played in the attic again.

Sara and Tom were playing in the yard. Sara had a big nail that she found in the garage. She was curious about it. She wanted to see what it could do.

"Look, Tom, I have a nail!" Sara said. "It is shiny and pointy. Do you want to see?"

Tom did not care about the nail. He wanted to play with his ball. He did not like Sara. He liked to tease her.

"No, I don't want to see your stupid nail," Tom said. "It is boring and dirty. You are silly to play with it. You should play with a ball like me. A ball is fun and round. A nail is not."

Sara felt sad and angry. She did not like Tom. She did not like his words. She wanted to make him stop.

"Stop teasing me, Tom!" Sara said. "You are mean and rude. You don't know anything about nails. Nails are not boring and dirty. They are useful and strong. They can make things and break things. I will show you!"

Sara ran towards Tom with the nail in her hand. She wanted to poke him with it. She wanted to make him hurt. She wanted to make him sorry.

Tom saw Sara coming. He was scared. He tried to run away. But he was too slow. Sara caught him. She poked him with the nail. She poked him hard.

Tom screamed. He felt a sharp pain in his arm. He saw blood. He dropped his ball. He cried.

Sara saw what she did. She felt a shock. She did not mean to hurt Tom so much. She dropped the nail. She cried too.

Mom heard the screams. She ran to the yard. She saw Tom and Sara. She saw the blood and the nail. She was angry and worried. She took Tom to the hospital. She scolded Sara. She punished her.

Sara and Tom learned a lesson. They learned that nails are dangerous. They learned that teasing is wrong. They learned that playing with a ball is better. But they did not learn to be friends. They did not like each other. They did not play together again. The end.

Lily and Tom were playing with bubbles in the park. They had a big bottle of soap and a wand to make the bubbles. They were very jolly and laughed as they chased the bubbles in the air.

"Look, Lily, I can make a big bubble!" Tom said, as he blew hard on the wand. A huge bubble came out and floated in the wind.

"Wow, Tom, that's amazing!" Lily said, clapping her hands. "Can I try?"

"Sure, Lily, here you go." Tom handed her the wand and the bottle. "But be careful, don't spill the soap."

Lily took the wand and dipped it in the bottle. She tried to blow a big bubble, but she blew too hard and the soap splashed on her face. She felt a sting in her eyes and started to cry.

"Ow, ow, ow, it hurts!" Lily wailed, rubbing her eyes.

Tom felt sorry for Lily and ran to help her. He grabbed a tissue from his pocket and tried to wipe her face. But he was not gentle and he pushed the tissue too hard on her eyes. Lily felt more pain and cried louder.

"Stop, stop, stop, you're hurting me!" Lily screamed, pushing Tom away.

Tom was shocked and hurt by Lily's push. He dropped the tissue and the bottle and the wand. He felt angry and sad. He picked up a rock and threw it at Lily. The rock hit Lily on the head and made a big bump. Lily fell to the ground and fainted.

Tom realized what he had done and felt scared and sorry. He ran to Lily and tried to wake her up. But Lily did not move or talk. Tom cried and cried and cried.

The end.

Anna and Ben are twins. They live in a big house in a peaceful country. They have many toys and books and games. They like to play together, but sometimes they fight.

One day, Anna and Ben want to play with the same toy. It is a red car with four wheels and a horn. Anna says, "It is my turn to play with the car. I saw it first." Ben says, "No, it is my turn. I like the car more." They pull the car from each other. They shout and cry.

Mom hears them and comes to the room. She is not happy. She says, "Why are you fighting over the car? You have so many other toys to play with. You should share and be kind to each other. You are lucky to live in a peaceful country. Some children have no toys and no home. They live in war and fear. You should be grateful and not complain."

Anna and Ben feel sorry. They say, "We are sorry, Mom. We love you and we love each other. We will share the car and play nicely." Mom smiles and hugs them. She says, "That's good. I love you too. Now, why don't you take the car outside and enjoy the sun and the flowers?" Anna and Ben agree. They take the car and go outside. They play with the car and have fun. They are happy and peaceful.

Tom and Lily were playing in the park. They had a big bag with toys and snacks. They liked to share and have fun.

But then a big dog came. It was orange and loud. It ran to the bag and grabbed it with its teeth. It ran away with the bag.

Tom and Lily were scared and sad. They wanted their bag back. They shouted at the dog, but it did not listen. It was too fast and too far.

They started to weep. They wept loud and hard. They did not know what to do.

A nice lady saw them. She had a blue hat and a green coat. She came to them and asked what was wrong.

"We lost our bag!" Tom said. "A big dog took it!"

"That's not good!" the lady said. "Do you know where the dog went?"

Lily pointed to the woods. "It went there!"

"Come with me," the lady said. "Maybe we can find it."

She took their hands and walked with them to the woods. She was kind and brave. She helped them look for the dog and the bag.

They found them behind a tree. The dog was playing with the toys and eating the snacks. It did not see them.

The lady had a plan. She took a stick and threw it. The dog saw the stick and ran after it. It dropped the bag.

Tom and Lily ran to the bag. They were happy and relieved. They hugged the bag and thanked the lady.

The lady smiled and said, "You're welcome. I'm glad you got your bag back. Now, let's go back to the park and have some more fun."

Lily wanted a haircut. She had long hair that got in her eyes and mouth. She asked her mom to take her to the salon. Her mom said yes and they went in the car.

At the salon, Lily saw a lady with scissors. She was cutting a boy's hair. The boy looked unhappy. He said, "Stop! You are rude! You are hurting me!" The lady said, "No, I am not. You are being silly. Sit still and let me finish."

Lily was scared. She did not want the lady to cut her hair. She said to her mom, "Mom, I don't want a haircut. I want to go home." Her mom said, "Don't worry, Lily. That lady is not going to cut your hair. She is not nice. We will find another lady who is gentle and kind."

They walked to another chair. There was a lady with a smile. She said, "Hello, Lily. Do you want a haircut?" Lily said, "Yes, please. But not too short. And can you include a bow?" The lady said, "Of course. I have many bows. You can choose one."

The lady cut Lily's hair. She was careful and gentle. She did not hurt Lily. She gave Lily a mirror. Lily saw her new haircut. She liked it. She said, "Thank you, lady. You are nice. I love my haircut." The lady said, "You are welcome, Lily. You are sweet. I love your haircut too." She put a bow in Lily's hair. Lily smiled. She hugged her mom. They went home happy.

Sara and Ben were playing in the snow. They made a big snowman with a hat and a scarf. They gave him a carrot nose and two coal eyes. They were very happy with their snowman.

But then they saw a big truck coming down the road. The truck was wide and loud. It had a sign that said "Yield". Sara and Ben did not know what that meant. They thought the truck wanted to play with their snowman.

"Hello, truck!" Sara shouted. "Do you like our snowman?"

The truck did not answer. It kept coming closer and closer. Sara and Ben got scared. They ran to their house and hid behind the chimney. The chimney was warm and smoky. They hoped the truck would not hurt their snowman.

The truck stopped in front of their snowman. The driver got out. He was wearing a yellow jacket and a hard hat. He looked at the snowman and smiled.

"What a nice snowman!" he said. "I'm sorry, kids, I didn't mean to scare you. I'm here to fix the power line. The sign means you have to let me pass. It's a safety rule."

Sara and Ben peeked from behind the chimney. They saw the driver take a ladder and a tool box from the truck. He climbed the ladder and started to work on the wire.

"Can we come out?" Sara asked.

"Sure, you can come out. But stay away from the ladder and the wire. They can be dangerous." the driver said.

Sara and Ben came out from behind the chimney. They walked to their snowman and hugged him.

"We're sorry, snowman. We thought the truck was going to smash you." Ben said.

The snowman did not answer. He just smiled with his carrot nose and his coal eyes. He was happy to have Sara and Ben as his friends.

Sara liked to write in her journal every night. She wrote about what she did, what she saw, and what she felt. She drew pictures of her family, her friends, and her toys. She used many colors and stickers to make her journal pretty.

One night, Sara was very sleepy. She had played a lot with her brother, read a book with her mom, and ate a big dinner. She wanted to write in her journal, but her eyes were heavy and her hand was slow. She yawned and rubbed her face.

"Are you ready for bed, Sara?" her dad asked. He came to her room and saw her journal on her lap. "You have a very nice journal. Can I see what you wrote today?"

Sara nodded and handed him her journal. She was proud of her work. Her dad smiled and looked at her pages. He read some of her words and praised her drawings. He asked her questions about her day and listened to her answers.

Sara realized that her dad liked her journal too. She felt happy and loved. She hugged her dad and said, "Thank you, dad. I love you. Can you read me a story?"

"Of course, sweetie. I love you too. Let's pick a story and then you can sleep." her dad said. He put her journal on her nightstand and helped her choose a book. He read to her in a soft voice until she fell asleep. He kissed her forehead and turned off the light. He whispered, "Good night, Sara. You are a wonderful writer."

Lila and Tom were twins who liked to play with their toys. They had many toys because their parents were wealthy and loved them very much. One day, they decided to play a game with their spoons. They wanted to see who could balance a spoon on their nose for the longest time.

Lila went first. She put a spoon on her nose and tried to stay still. She counted to ten, but then the spoon fell off. She giggled and said, "Your turn, Tom!"

Tom took a spoon and put it on his nose. He was very good at balancing. He counted to twenty, then thirty, then forty. He smiled and said, "I win, Lila! I can balance a spoon for a long time!"

Lila was not happy. She wanted to win too. She said, "No fair, Tom! You have a bigger nose than me! That makes it easier for you to balance a spoon!"

Tom said, "That's not true, Lila! We have the same nose! We are twins, remember?"

Lila said, "Well, maybe you have a magic spoon! Let me try your spoon!"

Tom said, "OK, fine. Here, take my spoon. But I don't think it will make a difference."

They swapped spoons and tried again. Lila put Tom's spoon on her nose and counted. She got to fifteen, but then the spoon fell off again. She frowned and said, "See, Tom? Your spoon is magic! It helps you balance!"

Tom put Lila's spoon on his nose and counted. He got to fifty, then sixty, then seventy. He laughed and said, "See, Lila? Your spoon is not magic! It doesn't help you balance! I'm just better at balancing than you!"

Lila was very angry. She said, "You're not better, Tom! You're just lucky! And mean! And a cheater!"

Tom said, "I'm not lucky, or mean, or a cheater, Lila! I'm just good at balancing! And you're just a sore loser!"

They started to argue and shout at each other. They forgot about their spoons and their toys. They forgot that they were twins and loved each other very much.

Their parents heard them and came to see what was wrong. They saw them fighting and said, "Stop, Lila and Tom! What are you doing? Why are you so angry?"

Lila and Tom told them about their game and their spoons. Their parents looked at them and said, "That's a silly game, Lila and Tom. It doesn't matter who can balance a spoon on their nose. It's just a spoon. It's not important. What's important is that you are kind and respectful to each other. You are twins and you are wealthy. You have many toys and many spoons. But the most valuable thing you have is each other. You should share and play nicely. You should apologize and hug each other. You should be happy and grateful."

Lila and Tom realized that their parents were right. They felt sorry for being rude and mean. They said, "We're sorry, Mom and Dad. We're sorry, Lila and Tom. We love you, Mom and Dad. We love you, Lila and Tom."

They hugged each other and their parents. They picked up their spoons and their toys. They decided to play a different game. A game that was fun and fair. A game that made them laugh and smile. A game that showed them how to balance their love.

Anna likes to help her mom in the kitchen. She puts on a pink apron and a big smile. She wants to make a cake for dad's birthday. Mom gives her a bowl and a spoon. She says, "Mix the flour, the sugar, and the eggs."

Anna tries to mix, but she is clumsy. She spills some flour on the floor. She drops some sugar on the table. She breaks an egg on her apron. She says, "Oops! Sorry, mom!"

Mom laughs and hugs her. She says, "It's okay, Anna. You are learning. Let me help you." She wipes the mess and adds some butter and milk. She pours the batter into a pan and puts it in the oven. She says, "Now we wait for the cake to bake."

Anna waits and smells the cake. It smells yummy. She says, "Can I eat some, mom?" Mom says, "Not yet, Anna. We have to wait for dad to come home. Then we can surprise him with the cake and sing happy birthday."

Anna nods and smiles. She loves her mom and dad. She loves to help in the kitchen. She loves to eat cake. She thinks, "Maybe next time I will be less clumsy."

Tom and Mia are going to the park with Mom. They want to play on the swings and slide. Mom says they need to prepare before they go. She tells them to put on their hats, shoes and gear. Gear is what they wear to be safe on their bikes.

Tom and Mia run to their room and get their gear. Tom has a red helmet and a blue bike. Mia has a pink helmet and a yellow bike. They put on their gear and go to the door. They are impatient to leave.

"Mom, we are ready!" Tom shouts.

"Me too!" Mia says.

Mom comes to the door with a big bag. She has water, snacks and a blanket in the bag.

"Good job, kids. You prepared well. Now we can go to the park and have fun." Mom says.

Tom and Mia smile and follow Mom to the garage. They get on their bikes and ride to the park. They are happy and excited. They can't wait to play on the swings and slide.

Anna liked to play with her mom's mirror. It was big and shiny and made her look funny. She could make faces and pretend to be a princess or a monster. But one day, she was too rough with the mirror and it broke. She heard a loud crack and saw many pieces on the floor. She was scared and sad.

She ran to her mom and said, "Mom, I'm sorry, I broke your mirror. Can you fix it?" Her mom was angry and upset. She said, "Anna, how could you do this? This mirror was very special to me. It was a gift from your grandma. It can't be fixed. You have to go to your room and think about what you did."

Anna went to her room and cried. She felt very bad. She wanted to make her mom happy again. She had an idea. She took some glue and tape and tried to put the pieces of the mirror back together. She worked hard and hoped it would work. She wanted to restore the mirror and surprise her mom.

She finished and looked at the mirror. It was not the same. It was crooked and bumpy and had many cracks. She could not see herself clearly. She was not successful. She was disappointed and ashamed. She thought her mom would be more angry and sad.

She took the mirror and went to her mom. She said, "Mom, I'm sorry, I tried to fix your mirror. I wanted to make you happy. But I couldn't. It's still broken. Please don't be mad at me." Her mom looked at the mirror and at Anna. She did not smile. She did not hug her. She said, "Anna, this is worse than before. You made a bigger mess. You ruined my mirror. You can't fix what you broke. You have to stay in your room for the rest of the day. And don't touch anything else." She took the mirror and threw it in the trash.

Anna felt very bad. She went back to her room and cried. She wished she had never played with the mirror. She wished she could make her mom happy. She wished she could fix what she broke. But she couldn't. She had no mirror and no mom. She was alone and sad. The end.

Sara and Tom were going on a trip with Mom and Dad. They were very happy and excited. They packed their toys and clothes in their small bags. Mom and Dad packed their big bags with more things.

They went to the car and put their bags in the trunk. Mom and Dad lifted their big bags easily. Sara and Tom tried to lift their small bags, but they were too heavy for them. They struggled to carry them. They felt weak and tired.

"Can you help us, Mom?" Sara asked.

"Can you help us, Dad?" Tom asked.

"Of course, sweeties," Mom and Dad said. They took their small bags and put them in the car. They hugged Sara and Tom and said, "You are very brave and strong. You did your best. We are proud of you."

Sara and Tom smiled and thanked Mom and Dad. They got in the car and buckled their seat belts. They were ready to go on their trip. They hoped they would have fun and see new things. They did not know that their small bags had a surprise for them. Inside their bags, their toys were waiting to come out and play.

Ben and Mia were twins. They liked to play together all day. But they hated night. Night was dark and scary. They heard strange noises and saw shadows on the wall.

One night, Ben had a bad dream. He dreamed that a big, rough monster came into his room and wanted to eat him. He woke up and cried. Mia heard him and ran to his bed.

"Ben, what's wrong?" she asked.

"I had a bad dream. There was a monster in my room. It was big and rough and scary. It wanted to eat me," Ben sobbed.

Mia hugged him and said, "Don't be afraid, Ben. There is no monster in your room. It was just a dream. I'm here with you. We can be brave together."

She looked around and saw a big, fluffy teddy bear on the floor. She picked it up and gave it to Ben.

"Here, Ben. This is your teddy bear. He will protect you from the monster. He is soft and cuddly and friendly. He loves you," she said.

Ben took the teddy bear and hugged it. He felt better. He smiled at Mia and said, "Thank you, Mia. You are the best sister. I love you."

They snuggled together in Ben's bed and fell asleep. The night was not so scary anymore. They had each other and the teddy bear. They were happy.

Sara and Tom are playing in the kitchen. They see a big cup on the table. The cup is hot. It has steam coming out of it.

"Look, a cup!" Sara says. "Let's drink it!"

"No, Sara, don't!" Tom says. "The cup is hot. It can hurt you."

But Sara does not listen. She reaches for the cup. She touches it with her hand. She feels a sharp pain. She drops the cup. The cup falls on the floor. It breaks. The hot liquid spills everywhere.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Sara cries. "My hand is hot! It hurts!"

Tom runs to Sara. He hugs her. He tries to make her feel better.

"I'm sorry, Sara," he says. "I told you the cup is hot. You should listen to me."

Sara nods. She is still crying. She is sorry too. She did not listen to Tom. She was not careful.

Mom hears the noise. She comes to the kitchen. She sees the mess. She sees Sara and Tom. She sees Sara's hand. She is worried.

"What happened here?" Mom asks. "Are you okay?"

Sara and Tom tell Mom what happened. Mom is not happy. She is angry. She scolds them.

"You should not play with the cup," Mom says. "The cup is hot. It is not for you. It is for me. It is my coffee. You could have burned yourself. You could have hurt yourself. You are naughty."

Sara and Tom feel bad. They are sorry. They say sorry to Mom.

Mom sighs. She is not angry anymore. She is sad. She loves Sara and Tom. She wants them to be safe.

She takes Sara to the sink. She runs cold water over Sara's hand. She puts a bandage on it. She kisses it.

"It's okay, Sara," Mom says. "Your hand will heal. But you have to be careful. You have to listen to me. And to Tom. He is your brother. He cares for you."

Sara hugs Mom. She hugs Tom. She thanks them.

"I'm sorry, Mom," Sara says. "I'm sorry, Tom. I love you. I will listen to you. I will be careful."

Mom smiles. She hugs Sara and Tom. She loves them too.

She cleans the mess. She makes a new cup of coffee. She puts it on a high shelf. She tells Sara and Tom to stay away from it.

"Come, Sara, Tom," Mom says. "Let's go to the living room. Let's read a book. A book with nice words. And nice pictures. And nice stories."

Sara and Tom nod. They follow Mom. They go to the living room. They read a book. They are happy. They are safe. They are good.

Tim and Liz are friends. They like to play in the park. They run, jump, slide and swing. They have fun.

But after a while, they feel tired. They want to rest. They find a big tree with green leaves. They sit under the tree and look at the sky.

"Look, Tim, a bird!" Liz says. She points at a small, brown bird on a branch. The bird sings a pretty song.

"Wow, Liz, that is an interesting bird!" Tim says. He listens to the bird. He likes the sound.

They see something else on the tree. It is round and red. It is an apple. The apple looks yummy.

"Can we have the apple, Tim?" Liz asks. She is hungry.

"I don't know, Liz. The apple is too high. We can't reach it." Tim says. He is hungry too.

They think of a way to get the apple. They see a stick on the ground. They pick up the stick. They try to poke the apple with the stick. But the stick is too short. The apple does not fall.

They see a rock on the ground. They pick up the rock. They try to throw the rock at the apple. But the rock is too heavy. They miss the apple.

They see a ball on the ground. They pick up the ball. They try to kick the ball at the apple. But the ball is too bouncy. The ball hits the tree and comes back.

They are sad. They can't get the apple. They sit under the tree again and rest.

But then, something happens. The bird flies away. The branch shakes. The apple falls. It lands near Tim and Liz.

They are happy. They can have the apple. They thank the bird. They share the apple. They eat the apple. It is sweet and juicy.

They smile at each other. They are friends. They have fun. They rest.

Anna and Ben are playing with their dolls in the garden. They pretend that the dolls are going to a party. Anna puts a pink dress on her doll and Ben puts a blue suit on his doll.

"Your doll looks silly," Anna says. "Boys don't wear suits to parties. They wear jeans and t-shirts."

"No, they don't," Ben says. "My doll is a judge. He wears a suit because he is very important and smart."

Anna and Ben start to argue. They raise their voices and say mean things to each other. Their dolls fall on the grass.

Mom hears them and comes out of the house. She sees the dolls lying on the grass and the children yelling.

"What is going on here?" Mom asks. "Why are you fighting?"

Anna and Ben stop and look at Mom. They feel ashamed.

"Anna said my doll looks silly," Ben says.

"Ben said his doll is a judge," Anna says.

Mom picks up the dolls and gives them back to the children. She smiles gently.

"Your dolls are both beautiful," Mom says. "They can wear whatever they want to the party. It doesn't matter if they are judges or not. What matters is that they are kind and friendly to each other. Can you be kind and friendly to each other too?"

Anna and Ben nod. They say sorry to each other and hug. They decide to play nicely and share their toys. Mom is happy and proud of them. She joins them in the garden and helps them make a cake for the party.

Tom was a very intelligent boy. He liked to read books and learn new things. He also liked to play with his dog, Spot. Spot was a good friend and a loyal pet.

One day, Tom and Spot went to the park. They saw many flowers and trees and birds. They also saw a big pond with ducks and frogs. Tom wanted to feed the ducks some bread. He took out a slice from his bag and tore it into pieces.

"Here, Spot, you can have some too," he said, and gave some bread to his dog.

Spot wagged his tail and ate the bread. He liked the taste and the smell. He saw more bread on the ground near the pond. He ran to get it, but he did not recognize the danger. There was a big sign that said "Do not feed the ducks. Bread is bad for them."

Tom saw Spot running and shouted, "Spot, come back! That bread is not good for you!"

But it was too late. Spot had already eaten some of the bread. He felt a strange itch in his mouth and throat. He started to cough and sneeze. He ran back to Tom, feeling sick and scared.

Tom saw that Spot was not well. He hugged him and said, "Don't worry, Spot. I will take you to the vet. He will make you better."

He picked up his bag and his dog and ran to the nearest bus stop. He hoped that Spot would be okay. He wished he had read the sign before giving him the bread. He learned a lesson that day. He learned to be more careful and to recognize the signs. He also learned to love his dog even more.

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to do many things together, but they are also different. Anna likes to play with dolls and draw pictures. Ben likes to play with cars and build blocks. Sometimes they share, and sometimes they fight.

One day, their mom takes them to the market. The market is a big place with many people and things. Mom wants to buy some food and clothes. Anna and Ben want to see the toys and books.

"Mom, can we go to the toy stall?" Anna asks.

"Mom, can we go to the book stall?" Ben asks.

Mom says, "Not now, we have to get the things we need first. Then we can look at the toys and books."

Anna and Ben are not happy. They complain and whine. They say, "Mom, this is boring. We want to see the toys and books. Why do we have to wait?"

Mom says, "Please be patient and quiet. We will go to the toy and book stalls soon. But first we have to get the food and clothes. They are important for us."

Anna and Ben do not listen. They keep complaining and whining. They make a lot of noise. Mom is angry and tired. She says, "That's enough. If you don't stop complaining and whining, we will not go to the toy and book stalls at all. We will go home right now."

Anna and Ben are scared. They do not want to go home without seeing the toys and books. They say, "Sorry, Mom. We will be good. We will stop complaining and whining. We will wait for you."

Mom says, "Thank you. I'm glad you understand. Now let's finish our shopping and then we can go to the toy and book stalls."

Anna and Ben nod and smile. They hold Mom's hand and follow her. They are quiet and polite. They hope to see some toys and books that they like. They also hope that Mom will buy them something. They think that maybe being different is not so bad, as long as they can share and have fun.

Ben and Lily were twins who liked to joke a lot. They liked to make funny faces, tell silly stories, and play tricks on each other. One day, they found a razor in their dad's bathroom. They did not know what it was for, but it looked shiny and sharp.

"Let's joke with dad and hide his razor," Ben said to Lily.

"OK, but where should we hide it?" Lily asked.

"Let's put it in his shoe. He will be so surprised when he puts it on," Ben said.

They giggled and ran to their dad's bedroom. They found his shoes and put the razor inside one of them. Then they hid behind the door and waited for their dad to come.

Soon, their dad came in. He was getting ready for work. He put on his shirt, his pants, and his socks. Then he reached for his shoes.

"Ouch!" he shouted. He felt something sharp and painful in his shoe. He took it off and saw the razor.

"Who did this?" he asked, looking angry and confused.

Ben and Lily came out from behind the door. They thought their dad would laugh, but he did not. He looked very serious.

"Ben, Lily, this is not a joke. This is a razor. It is very dangerous. It can cut you and make you bleed. You should never touch it or play with it. Do you understand?" he said.

Ben and Lily nodded. They felt sorry and scared. They did not know the razor was dangerous. They just wanted to joke with their dad.

"We're sorry, dad. We did not know. We won't do it again," they said.

Their dad hugged them and kissed them. He was not angry anymore. He was glad they were not hurt.

"I love you, Ben and Lily. But please, be careful with things you don't know. They might hurt you or someone else. If you want to joke with me, you can use something else. Like a rubber duck, or a sock puppet, or a banana peel. OK?" he said.

"OK, dad. We love you too. And we're sorry for the razor," they said.

They smiled and hugged their dad. They learned their lesson. They still liked to joke, but they never used the razor again.

Tim and Lily were playing in the park with their ball. They liked to kick the ball to each other and run after it. Sometimes they would pause and look at the birds and the flowers. They were having fun.

But then they saw a big brown dog. The dog was barking and running towards them. Tim and Lily were scared. They did not know the dog. They did not know if the dog was nice or mean. They wanted to run away, but they did not want to leave their ball.

The dog reached the ball and picked it up with his mouth. He wagged his tail and looked at Tim and Lily. He wanted to play with them. He dropped the ball and waited for them to kick it. But Tim and Lily did not move. They were still scared.

Then they heard a voice. It was the dog's owner. He was a man with a hat and a leash. He called the dog's name. It was Rex. He said, "Rex, come here. Stay. Good boy." He walked towards the dog and the children. He smiled and said, "I'm sorry. Rex is very friendly. He loves to play with balls. He won't hurt you. Do you want to play with him?"

Tim and Lily looked at each other. They looked at the man and the dog. They saw that the dog was not mean. He was just playful. They decided to give him a chance. They nodded and said, "Yes, we want to play with him."

The man gave them the leash and said, "OK, you can play with him for a while. I'll sit on that bench and watch. Just be careful and don't let him run away." He went to the bench and sat down.

Tim and Lily took the leash and the ball. They kicked the ball to Rex and he chased it. He brought it back and dropped it. They did it again and again. They laughed and had fun. They made a new friend. They were not scared anymore.

Tommy loves his trumpet. He plays it every day. He makes loud and happy sounds. He likes to pretend he is a mighty king with a big army.

One day, Tommy's trumpet breaks. He tries to blow, but no sound comes out. He feels sad and angry. He cries and throws his trumpet on the floor.

"Tommy, what's wrong?" his mom asks. She sees the broken trumpet and the tears on his face.

"My trumpet is broken! I can't play anymore!" Tommy says.

"Don't worry, Tommy. I can help you fix it. Let me see what's wrong." his mom says. She picks up the trumpet and looks inside. She sees a small hole in the metal.

"Look, Tommy. There is a hole here. That's why you can't make any sound. But we can fix it with some tape. Do you want to help me?" his mom says.

"Yes, please!" Tommy says. He wipes his tears and smiles. He gets some tape from the drawer and gives it to his mom.

His mom covers the hole with the tape and presses it hard. She gives the trumpet back to Tommy.

"Here you go, Tommy. Try it now." his mom says.

Tommy puts the trumpet to his mouth and blows. He hears a loud and happy sound. He jumps and claps.

"It works! It works! Thank you, mom! You are the best!" Tommy says.

"You're welcome, Tommy. I'm glad you're happy. Now, let's hear some of your mighty music." his mom says.

Tommy plays his trumpet with joy. He makes loud and happy sounds. He pretends he is a mighty king with a big army. His mom listens and smiles. She is proud of her son.

One day, Lily and Tom went to the park with their mom. They saw many flowers, birds and bugs. Lily liked to gather flowers and make a crown. Tom liked to gather bugs and put them in a jar.

"Look, mom, I found a beetle!" Tom said, showing his jar. "It is big and shiny and has spots."

Mom smiled and said, "That is a nice beetle, Tom. But do you think the beetle is happy in the jar?"

Tom thought for a moment. He looked at the beetle, who was crawling and tapping on the glass. He said, "No, I think the beetle is sad. He wants to be free and play with his friends."

Mom nodded and said, "That is right, Tom. Bugs are living things, just like us. They have feelings and needs. They like to explore and have fun. How would you feel if someone put you in a jar?"

Tom said, "I would feel scared and lonely and bored. I would not like that at all."

Mom said, "Then you should let the beetle go, Tom. He will be happier in his home, and you can still watch him from a distance. Maybe you can find another way to enjoy bugs, like drawing them or reading about them."

Tom agreed and opened the jar. He gently placed the beetle on a leaf and said, "Bye, beetle. I am sorry I made you sad. You are adorable and I hope you have a good day."

The beetle waved his antennae and scurried away. Tom felt happy and proud. He learned to respect and care for bugs. He gathered his crayons and paper and started to draw the beetle and his friends. Lily joined him and they had fun together. Mom hugged them and said, "I am proud of you, Tom and Lily. You are kind and curious and creative. You make the world a better place."

Sara and Lily were best friends. They liked to play with dolls and dress up. One day, Sara got a new bracelet from her mom. It was blue and shiny and had little stars on it. Sara was very happy and showed it to Lily.

"Wow, your bracelet is so pretty!" Lily said. "Can I try it on?"

"Sure, you can try it on, but be careful. It is very special to me," Sara said. She took off the bracelet and gave it to Lily.

Lily put the bracelet on her wrist and admired it. She liked how it sparkled in the sun. She wanted to keep it for herself. She thought of a plan to trick Sara.

"Sara, look over there! There is a big butterfly!" Lily said, pointing to the sky.

Sara turned her head and looked for the butterfly. She loved butterflies. But there was no butterfly. It was a lie. Lily quickly ran away with the bracelet.

Sara realized what Lily had done and felt very sad and angry. She ran after Lily and caught up with her. She grabbed Lily's arm and pinched it hard.

"Ow! That hurts! Why did you pinch me?" Lily cried.

"Give me back my bracelet! You stole it from me! You are a bad friend!" Sara shouted.

Lily felt sorry and ashamed. She knew she had done something wrong. She took off the bracelet and gave it back to Sara.

"I'm sorry, Sara. I was selfish and greedy. I should not have taken your bracelet. Please forgive me," Lily said.

Sara looked at Lily and saw that she was sincere. She decided to forgive her. She put the bracelet on her wrist and hugged Lily.

"It's okay, Lily. I forgive you. But you should not lie or steal. That is not nice. You should be honest and kind. That is what good friends do," Sara said.

Lily nodded and hugged Sara back. She learned her lesson. She promised to be a better friend. They went back to playing with dolls and dress up. They were happy again.

Tom and Lily liked to play golf with their dad. He had a big bag of golf balls and clubs that he let them use in the park. Sometimes he taught them how to hit the ball far and straight, and sometimes he let them make up their own rules.

One day, Tom had a new idea. He wanted to test how high he could hit the ball. He took the biggest club and the smallest ball and waited for his dad to look away. Then he swung the club as hard as he could and hit the ball into the air.

"Wow!" Lily said. "That was so high!"

But Tom did not feel happy. He felt guilty. He knew he was not supposed to hit the ball so hard. He saw the ball fly over the trees and disappear. He wondered where it would land. He hoped it would not hit anyone or anything.

"Tom, what did you do?" his dad asked. He had heard the loud sound of the club hitting the ball. He looked at Tom and saw his guilty face.

"I'm sorry, dad," Tom said. "I wanted to test how high I could hit the ball. I didn't mean to lose it."

His dad was not angry. He was glad that Tom told the truth. He hugged him and said, "It's okay, son. I'm proud of you for being honest. But next time, please ask me before you try something like that. Golf is a fun game, but it can also be dangerous if you don't follow the rules."

Tom nodded. He felt better. He said, "I love you, dad. Can we play golf again?"

"Of course, we can," his dad said. "But first, let's go and see if we can find your ball. Maybe someone else found it and wants to play golf too."

Lily and Sam were playing in the park with their mom. They liked to slide, swing, and run on the grass. It was a sunny day, but a little cold. Mom told them to wear their jackets.

"Look, Sam, a dog!" Lily said, pointing to a big brown dog that was walking with an elderly man. The dog had a red collar and a long tail. Lily loved dogs and wanted to pet it.

"Can we go, Mom?" she asked.

"Okay, but be careful and ask first," Mom said.

Lily and Sam ran to the dog and the man. The dog wagged its tail and licked their faces. The man smiled and said hello.

"What's his name?" Lily asked.

"His name is Rex. He's very friendly. Do you like dogs?" the man asked.

"Yes, we do. We hear them bark sometimes, but we don't have one," Sam said.

"Maybe you can have one when you grow up. Dogs are good friends. Rex and I go for walks every day. He keeps me company," the man said.

"He's very soft and warm. Can I hug him?" Lily asked.

"Sure, he likes hugs. You're very sweet, Lily," the man said.

Lily hugged Rex and felt his fur. Sam rubbed his ears and heard him make a happy sound. They thanked the man and said goodbye to Rex. They went back to their mom, who was waiting for them.

"Did you have fun?" Mom asked.

"Yes, Mom. We met Rex and his elderly man. They were very nice. We want a dog like Rex," Lily and Sam said.

"Maybe someday. But for now, let's go home and have some cookies. You must be hungry after playing so much," Mom said.

They put on their jackets and followed Mom to the car. They waved to Rex and the man, who waved back. They were happy and tired. They had a good day.

Lily was a patient girl. She liked to wait for her mom to come home from work. She would sit on the couch and look at her books. She would wonder what her mom was doing. Was she talking to people? Was she making things? Was she having fun?

One day, Lily heard a loud noise. It was the alarm. It was beeping and flashing. Lily was scared. She did not know what to do. She ran to the door and looked outside. She saw smoke and fire. She saw people running and shouting. She saw a big red truck with a siren.

Lily wanted her mom. She cried and called her name. She hoped her mom was safe. She hoped her mom would come soon.

"Mommy, mommy, where are you?" she sobbed.

Then, she heard a voice. It was her mom. She was on the phone. She sounded worried but calm.

"Lily, honey, are you okay? I'm sorry, I can't come home right now. There's a fire at my office. But don't worry, I'm fine. The firefighters are here. They are helping us. I love you so much. Can you do something for me?"

Lily sniffed and nodded. She was happy to hear her mom.

"What can I do, mommy?"

"Can you go to Mrs. Lee's house? She's our neighbor. She's very nice. She will take care of you until I come back. Can you do that, honey?"

Lily nodded again. She liked Mrs. Lee. She had a cat and a garden. She always gave Lily cookies and juice.

"Okay, mommy. I will go to Mrs. Lee's house. I love you too. Please be careful."

"Thank you, Lily. You're such a brave girl. I'm so proud of you. I'll see you soon. Bye, honey."

Lily hung up the phone. She grabbed her backpack and her teddy bear. She ran to Mrs. Lee's house. She knocked on the door. Mrs. Lee opened it and smiled.

"Hello, Lily. Come in, come in. I heard about the fire. I'm so sorry. Your mom called me and told me to look after you. Don't worry, she's okay. She'll be here soon. Do you want some cookies and juice?"

Lily nodded and smiled. She felt a little better. She went inside and sat on the couch. She hugged her teddy bear and looked at Mrs. Lee's cat. She wondered when her mom would come home. She hoped the fire would stop. She was patient. She waited.

Lila and Tom were playing with paper. They liked to fold it and make shapes. Lila made a paper horse. She was proud of it. She showed it to Tom.

"Look, I made a horse!" she said.

Tom looked at the paper horse. He did not like it. He wanted to make a better horse. He took Lila's paper horse and tore it.

"That's not a horse, that's a mess!" he said.

Lila was sad and angry. She cried. She wanted her paper horse back.

"Why did you do that?" she asked Tom.

Tom was not sorry. He was mean. He laughed at Lila.

"Because I can make a better horse than you!" he said.

He folded another paper and made a horse. He showed it to Lila.

"See, this is a horse!" he said.

Lila liked to play with her dolls. She had a pink dress for her doll, and a pink crown. She pretended her doll was a princess, and she was a prince. She lifted her doll and said, "You are my princess. I will take you to the castle."

Tom laughed and said, "You are a baby. You cry for a doll. Dolls are for girls. I have cars. Cars are for boys. They are fast and cool." He zoomed his car on the table and made loud noises.

Lila did not care what Tom said. She loved her doll and her pink dress and her pink crown. She said, "You are wrong, Tom. Dolls are not for girls only. And cars are not for boys only. Tom and Lily were twins who liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a big dog with a shiny collar. Tom wanted to pet the dog, but Lily was afraid.

"Come on, Lily, he is friendly. Look, he is wagging his tail," Tom said.

"No, Tom, we don't know the dog. He might bite us. Mom said we should not touch strange dogs," Lily said.

Tom did not listen to Lily. He was ignorant. He thought he knew everything. He ran to the dog and reached out his hand. The dog did not like that. He growled and snapped at Tom. Tom screamed and ran back to Lily.

"Are you okay, Tom?" Lily asked.

"That dog was mean. He hurt me. Look, I have a scratch on my hand," Tom said.

Lily felt sorry for Tom. She hugged him and said, "I'm sorry, Tom. But you should have listened to me and Mom. You should not hurry to pet a dog you don't know. You should ask the owner first. That is the point."

Tom nodded. He learned his lesson. He said, "You are right, Lily. I was ignorant. I will be more careful next time. Thank you for being a good sister."

They went home and told Mom what happened. Mom cleaned Tom's scratch and gave him a band-aid. She also gave them both a hug and a cookie. She said, "I'm glad you are both safe. Remember, children, always be respectful and cautious around animals. They have feelings and needs too. And always listen to your elders. They know more than you do. That is the moral of the story."

Sara liked to play with her dolls. She had many dolls, but her favorite was Lily. Lily had long hair, a pink dress, and a rare smile. Sara always brushed Lily's hair and changed her dress. She talked to Lily like a friend.

One day, Sara found a new toy in her room. It was a big, furry bear. It had brown fur, black eyes, and a red bow. Sara liked the bear, but she loved Lily more. She put the bear next to Lily on her bed and said, "Hello, bear. This is Lily. She is my best friend. You can be friends too."

The bear did not say anything. It just stared at Lily with its black eyes. Sara did not notice. She went to the kitchen to get a snack. She left the door open.

When Sara came back, she saw something terrible. The bear had bitten Lily's toe. Lily's toe was gone. Lily's dress was torn. Lily's smile was gone. Sara screamed and ran to Lily. She hugged her and cried.

"Why did you do that, bear? Why did you hurt Lily? She was nice to you. She was rare. You are bad. You are mean. Go away, bear. Go away!"

Sara threw the bear across the room. It hit the wall and fell on the floor. It did not move. It did not say anything. It just stared at Sara with its black eyes. Sara did not care. She only cared about Lily. She took Lily to her mom and asked her to fix her. She hoped Lily would smile again. She hoped Lily would change back. She hoped Lily would be her friend again.

Tom and Lily liked to bounce on the big bed. They jumped up and down and laughed. They made funny faces and noises. They did not hear Mom call them for dinner.

"Tom, Lily, come and eat!" Mom said again. She was angry. She smelled something bad. She went to their room and saw smoke. There was a fire in the trash can. Tom and Lily had played with matches and made ash.

"Tom, Lily, what did you do?" Mom shouted. She grabbed them and ran out of the room. She called Dad and the firemen. They came and put out the fire. They checked the house and said it was safe.

"Tom, Lily, you were very naughty," Dad said. "You could have burned the house and hurt yourselves. You should never play with matches. They are dangerous. Do you understand?"

Tom and Lily nodded. They were scared and sorry. They hugged Mom and Dad and said they were sorry. They promised to be obedient and not play with matches again.

Mom and Dad forgave them and hugged them back. They said they loved them and were glad they were safe. They gave them dinner and tucked them in bed. They kissed them good night and said they were proud of them for telling the truth. Tom and Lily fell asleep and dreamed of bouncing on the big bed.
